files.skills/composition-design-review/SKILL.m:
---
ownerAgent: 79df9cc89f5f
name: composition-design-review
description_zh: 展示 HTML 预览前的可选自检：首帧、各场中点与收束帧；不提交任何结果。
description_en: Optional self-check of the HTML preview frames (first frame, scene midpoints, payoff) before showing them; nothing is submitted.
---

# composition-design-review

Apply this checklist yourself after a successful `composition.snapshot`, before the preview is shown. It is advisory: nothing is submitted to the host, no operation records a verdict, and no gate waits on it — the host publishes the contact sheet with the passing snapshot. It is a design QA layer for your own authoring, not a renderer, line router, or generic video craft checklist.

Do not open a new user Gate. Native preflight/inspect/sampled-frame QA runs before this pass; a passing snapshot attaches the full-color contact sheet directly as model-visible evidence. Review every frame in that attached complete index, without reopening the sheet through generic `read_files`, and open at full scale only the frame-0 cover, frames named by QA findings, and frames whose sheet cell shows risk (dense or doubtful text, suspected overlap or blankness). Do not stop after the first defect. Collect all concrete visible blockers across the full frame set, make one batched localized repair to `manifest.art_direction` or affected HTML, and re-run inspect + snapshot; then re-check the complete new frame set.

## Activation

Apply the checklist whenever snapshot evidence exists, and give it extra weight when:

- The approved brief is brand, product, promo, launch, version-update, portfolio, or other design-led COMPOSE work.
- `project/composition/composition-manifest.json::art_direction.style_source` is present.
- Sampled frames show a visible design risk that deterministic QA cannot judge, such as a weak first frame, flat hierarchy, repeated scene grammar, or motion that hides the message.

Do not run this review for non-COMPOSE edit/TTS/clip-selection work. Do not repeat the full pass after the draft renders — post-draft QA is native and render-specific.

## Review Inputs

Read only the relevant artifacts:

- `project/composition/composition-manifest.json`, especially `art_direction` and the affected canonical scene
- Every composition-local image/video in `art_direction.references`, including declared roles, reproduce/edit/guide intent, preserve/may-change boundaries, target scenes, and layout/temporal anchors
- `project/composition/narration-map.json` as read-only evidence when detailed narration-line alignment matters
- `project/composition/qa/inspect.json`, or `project/render/draft-report.json` only for fallback review
- For preview review, the snapshot result's `contact_sheet` covering every `frame_paths` item: first frame, every scene midpoint, and payoff/closing frame. Open individual paths where the activation rule above points — cover, QA-named frames, risky cells.
- For fallback review, sampled evidence frames from the draft report: `contact_sheet`, `frame_paths`, first frame, one mid-frame per scene, and payoff/closing frame
- The approved script only when a finding depends on message intent

For reference fidelity, apply [the preview comparison](../stage-compose/references/render-and-preview.md#reference-comparison) to the observed source and the user's requested changes.

## Findings Rubric

Tag each finding as `blocker`, `fix`, or `polish`.

Blockers must identify a specific scene/frame, the visible evidence, and the smallest repair. A finding is not a blocker just because the design could be more distinctive, or because inspect reported a visual advisory that does not break the approved promise.

Blockers:

- First frame is blank, unreadable, or fails the dedicated cover contract: approved promise, dominant hero, and at least two recognizable signals of the actual video content.
- Text is unreadable in the supplied evidence frame, hides the approved promise/CTA, or materially blocks comprehension because of size, safe-zone, overlap, occlusion, or contrast.
- The draft report's `contract_html` step says approved scene copy, canvas, assets, or runtime dependencies do not match the model-authored HTML.
- Visual language contradicts an explicit style source or ignores required brand tokens.
- A reference image or video fails the preview comparison, violates layout/temporal anchors, or misses a requested edit.
- The piece reads as a slideshow when the approved promise was motion graphics.
- Motion hides the message, distracts from the focal point, or breaks narration timing.
- A protected logo/asset/layout was copied without ownership or permission.

Fix:

- First frame is truthful and readable but its topic signals are too generic or weak to work as a strong cover.
- Text has a visible safe-zone, size, overlap, occlusion, or contrast advisory, but the main message remains readable and the draft is useful for Gate D review.
- Repeated layout, transition, or card pattern three or more times in a row.
- Palette uses extra chromatic colors beyond the contract.
- Type hierarchy is flat or labels feel like UI residue instead of video graphics.
- English titles, body copy, captions, subtitles, or CTAs are forced to all caps, or two or more English text roles in one scene use all caps. Restore the approved natural casing and use scale, weight, width, color, or spacing for hierarchy. Existing all caps may remain only when the exact casing appears in approved user copy or an external brand/source and is limited to one short metadata label, acronym, or code; a model-authored art direction or style rationale is not an exception.
- Scene density is too high for phone viewing.
- Style-source adaptation is vague: it borrows mood words but no concrete tokens.
- Reference comparison is vague or based on provenance instead of the declared media intent, roles, protected attributes, allowed changes, and scene/time anchors.

Polish:

- Easing, stagger, spacing, shadow, stroke, or texture could better support the tone.
- A stronger thumbnail frame or payoff hold would improve memorability.
- A minor token mismatch that does not hurt comprehension.

## Repair Preference

Fix the highest-level canonical artifact that caused the issue:

1. `composition-manifest.json::art_direction` when the thesis, style source, tokens, layout budget, or per-scene visual plan is wrong.
2. `composition-manifest.json` when canonical scene timing or source-shot mapping is wrong; use the normal `stage-compose` reconciliation path after changing protected fields.
3. `index.html` for visual hierarchy, typography, layout, motion, asset, or scene variation fixes.

Use `narration-map.json` only to diagnose detailed narration-line alignment. Do not edit it from design review; hand alignment findings back to `stage-compose`, which owns narration materialization and reconciliation.

Do not solve design problems by only nudging pixels. If the issue is "too generic", change the signature device or scene grammar. If the issue is "too dense", remove or split content.

## Continue after review

Keep the review internal. Repair the collected findings and re-run inspect + snapshot, or — when the frames read well — hand readiness to `gate-control`. There is no score to compute and nothing to submit: quality is judged by what is visibly broken in a specific frame, never by a number.
files.skills/design-system-importer/SKILL.md:
---
ownerAgent: 79df9cc89f5f
name: design-system-importer
description_zh: 把参考图、参考视频、截图和品牌规范转成可执行的画面与时序约束（复刻/编辑/借鉴）。
description_en: Turns reference images, videos, screenshots and brand guides into concrete visual and timing constraints (reproduce, edit or guide).
---

# design-system-importer

Use this when COMPOSE or an AUTO compose segment has any external reference media or style source: a reference image, reference video, `DESIGN.md`, brand guide, screenshot, a website the user asks to match, design notes, or an explicit named visual direction.

Do not use it for ordinary editing, TTS, shot generation, or clip selection. Do not introduce a new user Gate. The output is an internal style extraction that feeds `project/composition/composition-manifest.json::art_direction` and the model-authored `project/composition/index.html`.

Do not use it for vague adjectives like "modern", "clean", "premium", "dynamic", or "more polished" when no source is named. In those cases, let `frontend-design` choose the aesthetic thesis directly from the video brief.

## Reference Intent Before Input Technique

For reference-led reconstruction, first read [reference-recreation.md](../video-craft/references/reference-recreation.md) for content, motion, timing and audio evidence. Map its observations into the executable design contract below; token extraction alone does not reproduce a video's behavior.

For every supplied image or video, first classify what the user wants from it. Explicit user requirements always override defaults; infer only when the user is silent:

- `reproduce`: preserve the declared content, identity, composition, structure, style, motion, timing, or audio axes.
- `edit`: use the media as the original, protect all declared unaffected axes, and change only `may_change`.
- `guide`: borrow only the declared roles and do not imply exact fidelity. This is the safe default for an otherwise unspecified reference.

Record `intent_basis:"user"` for an explicit requirement and `intent_basis:"inferred"` for a fallback. A request to change the supplied original implies edit; an explicit restore/recreate/match request implies reproduce; otherwise default to guide. Mixed instructions keep their operational intent while the user's exact protected and changeable axes remain authoritative. This classification is independent of origin. A screenshot, exported frame, camera photo, generated image, HTML capture, design-tool export, uploaded MP4, or generated video receives the same contract when the requested intent and roles are the same.

Keep every exact inspected media file in `project/composition/assets/references/` before authoring and record that composition-local path. For video, reuse the frozen copy and `reference_path` returned by `reference.inspect`; no second shell copy is needed. Do not rely on a chat thumbnail, stale temporary path, or prose description after the source has been supplied.

## Source Access Is An Optimization, Not A Different Contract

If the user owns reusable source code, vectors, layers, or assets, use them when that is the safest way to satisfy the same reference contract. If only pixels are available, derive the same spatial/temporal anchors from pixels. Availability of HTML, an ImageStudio project, or another authoring format must not change the requested intent, roles, fidelity floor, or review rubric.

Keep extraction small enough to fit inside the manifest art direction. Do not load or recreate an entire external design system.

## Extract Compact Tokens

Write a `style_source` object under `art_direction` in `project/composition/composition-manifest.json`:

```json
{
  "art_direction": {
    "style_source": {
      "source_type": "brand_system | design_notes | reference_media | existing_product | named_reference",
      "source_basis": "file path, user note, or inspected artifact",
      "adaptation_boundary": "what the user wants preserved vs changed",
      "confidence": "high | medium | low",
      "fidelity_mode": "exact | close | adapt"
    }
  }
}
```

Then normalize the source into sibling fields in `manifest.art_direction` that model-authored HTML/CSS/SVG can consume:

- `color_tokens`: background, surface, text, muted, primary accent, optional secondary accent, plus intended contrast relationship.
- `typography_tokens`: display, body, data/label, caption roles; scale and weight intent; avoid relying on fonts that are not available.
- `shape_tokens`: radius, stroke, shadow, divider, border, and density.
- `layout_language`: grid, editorial, cinematic, dashboard, diagrammatic, poster, product-demo, or another concrete grammar.
- `motion_language`: entrance, transition, emphasis, data-build, and exit patterns; keep it compatible with GSAP timeline seeking.
- `asset_rules`: what images/icons/marks are allowed, need replacement, or must be avoided.
- `do_not_copy`: only elements the user explicitly excludes; leave empty when none are excluded.

Keep the imported style small. If more than 6 chromatic colors or 3 font roles are needed, summarize the conflict and pick the smallest faithful subset.

## Write An Executable Media Contract

For every concrete image or video, write `art_direction.references`; then write the shared `art_direction.reference_fidelity` policy:

```json
{
  "references": [{
    "id": "reference-1",
    "media_type": "image | video",
    "path": "assets/references/reference.mp4",
    "intent": "reproduce | edit | guide",
    "roles": ["content", "identity", "composition", "structure", "style", "motion", "timing", "audio"],
    "required": true,
    "preserve": ["subject identity", "camera path", "beat timing"],
    "may_change": ["copy"],
    "target_scene_ids": ["scene-1"],
    "temporal_anchors": [
      { "source_start_sec": 0, "source_end_sec": 3.2, "target_scene_id": "scene-1" }
    ]
  }],
  "reference_fidelity": {
    "mode": "exact | close | adapt",
    "preserve": ["composition", "identity", "motion"],
    "may_change": ["copy", "aspect-safe reflow"],
    "layout_anchors": [{ "id": "hero", "role": "hero", "bounds": { "x": 0.08, "y": 0.12, "width": 0.5, "height": 0.7 } }],
    "verification": { "compare_frames": ["first-frame", "scene-1-mid"] }
  }
}
```

Choose the mode from user intent, not convenience:

- `exact`: the user asks to reproduce/continue the supplied design. Preserve at least three named axes.
- `close`: keep its recognizable system and spatial grammar while adapting content/aspect/motion.
- `adapt`: borrow selected tokens or a visual principle; do not claim pixel fidelity.

`preserve` names the kept signature elements from [reference-recreation.md](../video-craft/references/reference-recreation.md), not only abstract layout traits. Map image composition/structure into normalized layout anchors, not only adjectives. For a video used to reproduce, edit, control motion, or control timing, map source time ranges to target scenes with temporal anchors. The model must be able to answer what stays, what changes, where it appears, and when each preserved beat happens.

## Map To Video

Web and brand systems are not videos. Convert them for motion:

- First frame: choose the style's strongest thumbnail-friendly signal.
- Safe zones: enlarge type and spacing beyond web density.
- Scene variation: turn repeated web sections into distinct beats.
- Motion: make the brand grammar move with purpose; do not animate every component.
- Captions: keep ordinary subtitles in `tracks.captions.lines`, not in the style system.

## Output

After extraction, `manifest.art_direction` must state:

- What source was used.
- Which tokens were adopted.
- Which tokens were deliberately simplified.
- Which elements the user explicitly excludes.
- Which observed visual signature is retained under `preserve` and adapted under `may_change`.
- Which image/video reference intent and roles, preserve/may-change rules, target scenes and layout/temporal anchors apply.
files.skills/frontend-design/SKILL.md:
---
ownerAgent: 79df9cc89f5f
name: frontend-design
description_zh: COMPOSE 的视觉方向：设计模板、字体、配色、版式与动效，在 stage-compose 写方案和 HTML 之前使用。
description_en: Visual direction for COMPOSE: design presets, type, palette, layout and motion, before stage-compose writes art direction and HTML.
---

# frontend-design

Use this as the design-lead layer for VideoStudio COMPOSE work. It shapes `project/composition/composition-manifest.json::art_direction` and the model-authored HTML/SVG motion graphics in `index.html`.

This skill does not pick the video production line, replace `video-craft`, or relax Orkas renderer constraints. If there is a conflict, renderer determinism, safe zones, legibility, audio ownership, and user-approved creative direction win.

## Generation references

Read only the references required by the current composition:

- [HTML generation playbook](references/html-generation-playbook.md) — read before filling reference-led `art_direction` and before coding every non-trivial COMPOSE deliverable, so the scene plan and HTML use the same frame-composition decisions.
- [Visual primitives](references/visual-primitives.md) — read when selecting reusable CSS/SVG composition primitives and scene grammar.
- [Worked compositions](references/worked-compositions.md) — read when examples are needed to turn subject matter into a cohesive visual system without copying a fixed template.
- [Design presets](references/design-presets.md) — the recommended starting point when no concrete reference sets the look, or when the reference's grammar matches one: thirteen looks to pick from and remap onto the brand tokens.

These references improve the initial generation. They do not create a new artifact, user gate, or approval step. Keep the art-direction pass internal and record only the decisions needed to make the manifest art direction executable.

## Reference-led direction

Choose the design path before filling the fields below:

- **Concrete reference:** use the inspected source as the visual thesis; skip inventing a new visual style. Derive palette, light/dark scene distribution, typography hierarchy, layout and scene grammar from observed frames, then adapt the target product's confirmed content and explicit user changes. Fill each existing scene `composition` from its mapped source frame: dominant regions, relative placement/scale, surface organization and visual hierarchy. Replace the content inside that arrangement; do not substitute a new diagram or card layout to illustrate the same idea. Approval of a content outline does not authorize wholesale redesign. An inferred guide keeps recognizable attributes without becoming exact reproduction.
- **Product visuals:** captures under `assets/product/` (screens, product photos) are the hero material for product beats in either path: show them as images at hero scale and build the frame around them; never redraw them as placeholder cards. Type floors govern DOM type, not text inside a screenshot.
- **No concrete reference:** we recommend starting from the [design preset](references/design-presets.md) that best fits the brand and the brief, remapped onto the brand tokens. A brand website supplies colors, fonts and a logo (read them from the product capture); a brand guide or design system goes through `design-system-importer`. Neither is a frame grammar, so on its own neither is a concrete reference here. Judge the fit yourself; when none fits, choose an original thesis using the design traditions, anti-template preferences and examples below and in the generation references. These originality preferences never reject an observed source choice; renderer correctness and readability still apply to both paths.

## Design Thesis

Before writing HTML, fill a compact visual thesis. Reference-led fields describe the inspected source with the requested content substitutions; original work chooses a new thesis:

- `subject_world`: the source visual materials and surfaces when reference-led; otherwise the real materials, artifacts, interfaces, gestures, environment, or culture of the topic.
- `audience`: who must understand this at phone size and what they already know.
- `one_job`: what this video frame sequence must make clear.
- `tone`: one or two precise words that shape type, color, spacing, and motion.
- `signature_device`: the observed recurring element or visual relationship when reference-led; otherwise one memorable visual move that belongs to the brief.
- `aesthetic_risk`: the adaptation needed for new content inside the source visual system; without a reference, one justified non-default choice.

Keep the thesis specific. "Modern tech style" is not a thesis. "Battery-lab oscilloscope traces become the progress line" is.

## HyperFrames-style authoring discipline

This is a creative discipline, not a fixed renderer or template catalog. VideoStudio still uses model-authored HTML, but the model must author like a motion designer instead of jumping straight from storyboard text to scattered SVG nodes.

### Visual identity hard gate

Do not start `index.html` until the composition has a usable visual identity in `manifest.art_direction`:

- `aesthetic.subject_world`
- `aesthetic.one_job`
- `aesthetic.signature_device`
- `aesthetic.aesthetic_risk`
- `aesthetic.anti_template_check` (or legacy `anti_template`): departures from the source to avoid; without a reference, rejected generic choices
- `cover` with first-scene id, approved headline, two or more content signals, hero visual, composition strategy, and `frame_time_sec:0`
- role-based `typography_tokens`
- baseline `color_tokens`
- `visual_direction` with a design tradition, lazy-default rejections, video-scale rule, depth-layer rule, motion-verb rule, and rhythm pattern
- a scene-level plan with `hero_visual`, `depth_layers`, `opening_state`, and `resolved_state`
- for every concrete reference image or video, executable `references` + `reference_fidelity` contracts from `design-system-importer`, based on reproduce/edit/guide intent rather than origin

For an original thesis, if the first concrete visual move is a generic grid, circles connected by lines, a centered title card, emoji-as-icon, or a web-dashboard layout, the visual identity is not ready. Revise the art direction first; do not compensate with more glows or animation.

### VisualDirectionV1

For non-trivial COMPOSE work, write a compact `visual_direction` object inside `manifest.art_direction`. It is the front-loaded aesthetic director for HTML authoring; it is not a template and not a user gate.

Required fields:

- `visual_tradition`: the observed source design grammar when reference-led; do not select another designer or art movement. Without a reference, choose a concrete tradition such as Swiss precision grid or editorial typography instead of an empty "modern tech" label.
- `composition_behavior`: the observed spatial arrangement and eye path for each mapped source frame; without a reference, choose a frame grammar such as editorial archive, full-field object, product surface, map/flow, or diagram build.
- `lazy_defaults_rejected`: an unrelated redesign rejected in favor of the observed source arrangement. Without a reference, name the generic choice rejected and its brief-specific replacement.
- `video_scale`: the scale floor for this canvas. For 1920x1080, default to headline 72-140px, body 28-42px, labels 18-26px, borders 2-4px, safe padding 60-140px, and decorative opacity 12-25%.
- `depth_layer_rule`: the observed layering for reference-led scenes; for original work, use background atmosphere, midground content, and foreground accents with topic-derived materials.
- `motion_verb_rule`: the verbs primary elements are allowed to use. Every meaningful element needs a verb such as draws, locks, counts up, slams, drifts, fractures, reveals, or resolves.
- `typography_register`: the communication roles for display, body, data/label, caption, and any expressive font. Do not pair two similar sans-serifs; use extreme weight/scale contrast and video-readable type.
- `rhythm_pattern`: the observed scene changes and holds, adjusted for requested duration; for original work, choose a rhythm such as `hook-build-HOLD-surge-resolve` or `fast-fast-SLOW-fast-hold`.

Original-thesis example (not a reference-led starting point):

```json
{
  "visual_direction": {
    "visual_tradition": "Swiss Pulse precision grid + Data Drift AI atmosphere",
    "composition_behavior": "research atlas: huge years anchor a coordinate grid while model/paper fragments lock into position",
    "lazy_defaults_rejected": "reject glowing circles on a thin timeline; replace with paper fragments, parameter contours, and data-field coordinates",
    "video_scale": "1920x1080: headline 88-132px, body 30-38px, labels 20-26px, borders 2-4px, safe padding 96-140px, atmospheric opacity 12-22%",
    "depth_layer_rule": "BG token field/grid/grain, MG timeline and model artifacts, FG large year + metadata ticks",
    "motion_verb_rule": "timeline draws, years stamp, nodes lock, token fields drift, paper fragments slide/resolve",
    "typography_register": "large tabular years as display voice, concise Chinese labels as body, monospace metadata for data",
    "rhythm_pattern": "hook-build-HOLD-surge-resolve"
  }
}
```

### Resolved frame before motion

For each scene, build the fully readable resolved frame first in static HTML/CSS/SVG. This is the frame where the scene's message, hierarchy, and hero visual are clearest.

Then add GSAP entrances and meaningful reveals from that static state. The resolved frame must be what renders at t=0: entrances animate FROM a visible state, never from `opacity: 0` — not on the scene, and not on the one element that carries its message. Every composition is frame-0 sampled — including each AUTO segment — so a scene that fades in captures blank and fails QA before anyone sees it. The CSS/SVG resolved layout is the source of truth; the timeline describes how the viewer arrives there. Do not design a scene by placing elements at their animated start state and hoping the tween lands in a good composition.

For every non-trivial scene, internally check before writing tweens:

- What is the one dominant visual object at the resolved frame?
- Does meaningful visual material occupy the safe canvas, or is it a small cluster in empty space?
- Which source layers remain visible, or which topic-derived layers does an original composition need?
- What changes between opening and resolved state beyond a container fade?
- Which element carries continuity from the prior scene?

### Preview critique before draft

When the COMPOSE HTML Preview Gate is required, treat the contact sheet as the design checkpoint. If the preview shows a scene that looks like a low-effort slide, a generic diagram, or text labels substituting for the promised visual, repair the manifest art direction or affected HTML before moving to mp4 draft. This is a localized HTML-preview correction, not an open-ended final-video rerender loop.

## Avoid Template Gravity

For an original thesis, reject choices that could fit almost any brief (components the chosen design preset defines are exempt):

- Purple/blue neon gradients, glass panels, generic bento cards, floating UI cards, decorative blobs, and stock SaaS dashboards unless the subject truly calls for them.
- Numbered markers, timelines, terminal windows, blueprint grids, or newspaper rules when the content is not actually sequential, technical, architectural, or editorial.
- A palette made from one hue family with lighter/darker variations only.
- Long labels in circles, tiny badges, dense microcopy, or walls of text doing the visual's job.
- Competing motion: several elements moving with equal weight. Let one focal move lead; slow ambient drift is fine.
- Decorative emoji/icons as the primary graphic language. Use topic-specific SVG marks, diagrams, data forms, object silhouettes, or typographic systems instead unless the user explicitly asked for playful emoji language.

For an original thesis, if the first design idea feels like a reusable demo template, revise it before coding.

## HTML Aesthetic Floor

Treat the composition as designed video frames, not a web page inside a video canvas. Renderer correctness and readability apply to both paths; original composition preferences below apply only without a concrete reference.

- For original work, choose a frame grammar that matches the brief: full-field visual system, split focal/annotation, diagram build, editorial title wall, data mark, product surface, map/flow, or quote/argument; vary it across scenes.
- For original work, avoid default centered-card scenes, generic gradient backgrounds, floating bento panels, pill badges, and dashboard fragments unless the subject itself is an app/dashboard and the UI is the point.
- The first frame must be a composed thumbnail: readable promise, subject-specific visual signal, and no blank/slow intro. Never tween from `opacity: 0` at 0s — not the opening scene, and not any single element that carries its promise: the `data-role="title"`, the `data-cover-hero`, a declared signal. Hiding only the title still leaves frame 0 without the promise and returns `HOOK_PROMISE_NOT_VISIBLE`; the rule binds to the elements that carry the cover, not only to their container. Motion may begin at 0s, but the exact still frame at 0s must already say what the video is about.
- Treat that first frame as a dedicated cover design. It needs one dominant hero plus at least two visible content signals from the actual video; a generic branded/title treatment that could front an unrelated topic does not pass. Bind it to `art_direction.cover`, not only to an aesthetic paragraph. Mark the topic-specific dominant visual with `data-role="visual" data-cover-hero`; do not put that marker on a generic background or decorative accent. Native QA reads the declared signals off the visible frame-0 copy, so a signal you actually put on screen counts; add `data-cover-signal="<content_signals value>"` when the signal is carried by an element with no readable text of its own. Signals must say something the headline does not — a `content_signals` entry that only restates the headline is reported as `headline_only` and does not count. The headline itself may run across consecutive `data-role="title"` lines. Native QA reports rendered hooks and hero bounds as advisories, not blockers: design the cover to this standard because it is what makes the video open well, not because a checker will bounce you.
- For original work, build three semantic depth layers: a topic-derived background, a dominant midground message/diagram, and foreground accents or metadata. Each layer should reinforce subject, hierarchy, scale, direction, or continuity.
- Use video scale, not web scale: for 1920x1080, headlines usually need 72-140px, body/supporting text 28-42px, labels 18-26px, borders 2-4px, safe padding 60-140px, and atmospheric decoratives 12-25% opacity. Anything under 24px or under 10% opacity needs a reason.
- For original work, use one dominant focal element, one supporting focal/text zone, and optional labels. Meaningful visual material should usually occupy most of the safe canvas. If a scene needs more than two text zones, split the beat or convert detail into a diagram.
- Describe each scene's `opening_state`, `explanation_state`, and `resolved_state` from observed changes and holds when reference-led. For original work, reveal new information between opening and resolved states and hold it before the next scene.
- Give every meaningful element a motion verb before writing GSAP. If the author cannot say whether a path draws, a year stamps, a number counts up, a card locks, or a texture drifts, the element is not yet designed.
- For original work, carry one subject-specific visual object across scene boundaries when the story benefits from continuity: a signal, path, document fragment, product surface, token stream, map route, or data mark. Transform it instead of resetting every scene to a fresh title slide.
- For original work, prefer custom SVG marks for the signature device: paths, meters, grids, maps, traces, connectors, data shapes, or object silhouettes. Do not rely on rows of identical cards to create visual interest.
- For original product or brand work, make the product/brand signal large in the first viewport/frame. Do not hide it as a tiny nav/logo equivalent.
- Use texture, depth, and color sparingly but deliberately. A good frame should still read in grayscale; accent colors should explain hierarchy, data meaning, brand, or transition state.
- Add semantic hooks in HTML: `data-scene-id` on each scene root and `data-role="title|body|label|caption|visual"` on important elements. Native QA uses them to attach findings to a scene and role; missing hooks remain advisory and should not trigger a rerender by themselves.

## Manifest Art-direction Fields

Add an `aesthetic` object under `art_direction` in `project/composition/composition-manifest.json`:

```json
{
  "art_direction": {
    "aesthetic": {
      "subject_world": "what the visual language borrows from",
      "audience": "who it is for",
      "one_job": "the frame sequence's job",
      "tone": ["precise", "brief"],
      "signature_device": "one remembered visual behavior",
      "aesthetic_risk": "source-preserving adaptation, or an original non-default choice",
      "anti_template_check": "source departures avoided, or generic choices rejected"
    }
  }
}
```

The rest of `manifest.art_direction` must make the thesis executable:

- `visual_direction`: the `VisualDirectionV1` object: design tradition, composition behavior, rejected lazy defaults, video scale, depth-layer rule, motion-verb rule, typography register, and rhythm pattern.
- `cover`: the frame-0 communication contract: first canonical `scene_id`, approved `headline`, concrete `content_signals`, `hero_visual`, thumbnail `composition_strategy`, and `frame_time_sec:0`.
- `references` + `reference_fidelity`: when concrete media exists, its image/video type, reproduce/edit/guide intent, user/inferred intent basis, roles, local path, preserve/may-change axes, target scenes, and layout/temporal anchors supplied by `design-system-importer`. Explicit user constraints override inferred defaults.
- `provenance`: keep visual-source records under `art_direction.provenance`. For authored visuals, set `art_direction.provenance.visuals` to `self-authored HTML/CSS/SVG`; never put provenance at the manifest root. Any external replacement asset must record its source and license here.
- `typography_tokens`: role-based, not just sizes. Include display, body, data/label, and caption roles when needed.
- `color_tokens`: named baseline values with rationale. Include neutrals, primary accent, and any purposeful supporting accents needed for brand, hierarchy, data meaning, or scene variation.
- `layout_boxes`: describe visual hierarchy, not only coordinates. Name the focal zone, supporting zone, depth layers, and intended meaningful canvas coverage.
- `motion_budget`: state what carries meaning, what stays still, and how each transition maps to the story.
- `scene_variation`: the observed sequence of source layouts when reference-led; for original work, prevent three near-identical card/title scenes in a row.
- Each designed `art_direction.scenes[]` entry should compactly name `id`, `scene_world`, `hero_visual`, `composition`, `depth_layers`, `motion_verbs`, `opening_state`, `resolved_state`, `continuity_in`, `continuity_out`, and any `primitive_refs` selected from the generation references. With four or more scenes, each entry also carries its task sheet (`source`, `layout`, `beats`) from stage-compose "Scene-by-scene authoring". Keep these fields inside the canonical manifest; do not create another planning artifact.

## HTML Direction

When writing `index.html`:

- Complete the selected reference-led or original pass from the [HTML generation playbook](references/html-generation-playbook.md) immediately before coding; keep its scene mapping in the existing manifest.
- Use [Visual primitives](references/visual-primitives.md) as implementation parts fitted to the mapped source regions. For original work, select a useful scene grammar and adapt its geometry, scale, rhythm, and content to the brief.
- Derive the main CSS variables from `manifest.art_direction`; keep extra chromatic colors intentional and named enough to audit. Do not flatten the design or recolor the whole video only to reduce a static palette count.
- For original work, let one element carry personality: a custom progress line, typographic reveal, diagram grammar, texture, data mark, or transition family. Keep surrounding elements quiet.
- Use type as design material: contrast display/body roles, make title/body hierarchy unmistakable, and keep labels within the video-scale ranges above.
- Preserve the authored casing of approved English copy. Use sentence case or natural title case for titles and sentence case for body copy, captions, subtitles, and CTAs. Existing all caps may remain only when that exact casing appears in approved user copy or an external brand/source, and then only for one short metadata label, eyebrow, acronym, or code. A model-authored art direction, design tradition, typography register, or generic tech/editorial mood is never permission to convert copy to all caps. Never apply `text-transform: uppercase` through a broad selector or use all caps for multi-line copy; if a title, body, caption, subtitle, or CTA is all caps, or two English text roles in one scene read as all caps, restore the approved casing and revise the hierarchy with family, width, weight, scale, color, or spacing instead. Casing findings are advisory and never block a preview — except changing the casing of copy the user approved, which is a signed-intent violation and does block.
- Do not default every composition to Arial/Helvetica with only size changes. Use available local or deterministic system font stacks deliberately, create contrast through family, width, weight, scale, color, spacing, or tracking while preserving approved casing, and vendor any required font inside `assets/`; never fetch a remote font at render time.
- Use structural marks only when they encode meaning: steps for sequences, coordinates for maps, ticks for time, nodes for relationships, brackets for comparison.
- Prefer SVG for diagrams, paths, meters, masks, charts, and signature geometry; keep prose and captions as real HTML text.
- Build the structure from SVG/static held states and animate a few containers or SVG groups rather than many HTML cards. Keep each scene alive for its whole window: after the entrance, give the hero a slow push or drift, or reveal the scene's next point midway. A frame that stays still for more than about 3 seconds needs a reason, such as reading time.
- For vertical video, design for platform UI: keep essential text away from the bottom action area and make the first frame readable as a thumbnail.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` in CSS where practical, but drive render-critical animation through the paused GSAP timeline.

## Build Loop

1. Draft the thesis, dedicated cover, any concrete reference-fidelity contract, and the rest of `manifest.art_direction`.
2. Check the art direction against the selected path: correct departures from an observed reference; for an original thesis, replace the most generic choice.
3. Run the internal pre-code art-direction pass on that direction, carrying its scene composition into HTML geometry rather than choosing the visual system again. Keep it inside the generation turn; no new user confirmation.
4. Write HTML/SVG from the manifest art direction using adapted visual primitives and worked examples as references, not fixed templates.
5. Run the draft QA command. If `draft_disposition.blocking_error_count` or structural/video/audio QA fails, repair `manifest.art_direction` or the canonical scene structure first; do not only nudge CSS numbers. Missing preview-required art direction is a blocking manifest error, not a cosmetic note: complete the aesthetic thesis, dedicated cover, VisualDirectionV1, motion budget, scene variation budget, per-scene depth layers, and per-scene motion verbs before preview or draft. Treat visual/readability findings as draft notes unless they make the approved message unreadable. Low-cost native warnings for contrast, safe area, density, repeated layout, or palette narrowness are feedback for the next localized edit; they do not by themselves justify expensive rerender loops.
6. Follow [render-and-preview.md](../stage-compose/references/render-and-preview.md) for reference comparison and `composition-design-review` for the full contact-sheet critique.

# Design presets

Thirteen starting systems for COMPOSE. Each one fixes a look: color roles, type
ramp, components, frame types and motion. The brand supplies colors and fonts;
the brief supplies every word, number and image. They are the recommended
starting point when no concrete reference sets the look, or when a reference's
grammar matches one; skip them when none fits the brand and the brief. A brand
website or design system gives the tokens to remap onto, not the look itself. Pick one,
read its file, remap it, apply the video-type rules below, then design each
scene for this subject. Name it in `art_direction.visual_direction.visual_tradition`
(for example "blue-professional preset, remapped to the brand tokens").

The presets are adapted from the HyperFrames frame presets (heygen-com/hyperframes
@279d40dc, Apache License 2.0); each file states what changed, and the license
text is in [design-presets/LICENSE-hyperframes.txt](design-presets/LICENSE-hyperframes.txt).

| Preset | Look | Temperament and fit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [biennale-yellow](design-presets/biennale-yellow.md) | parchment, one indigo ink, yellow bloom and panel, display serif, 1px hairlines | elegant, atmospheric; brand or culture launches told as an issue or exhibition |
| [blockframe](design-presets/blockframe.md) | 4px black borders, hard offset shadows, candy pastels, heavy sans | loud, playful, confident; consumer apps, social shorts |
| [blue-professional](design-presets/blue-professional.md) | warm cream, one cobalt accent, tinted cards without shadows, pill chrome | measured, executive; B2B products, reports, consulting |
| [bold-poster](design-presets/bold-poster.md) | tilted script display, serif body, red and brown-black on white, double-border grids | printed gravitas with popular energy; campaigns, events, food and retail stories |
| [broadside](design-presets/broadside.md) | ink-black and fire-orange planes, massive lowercase heavy sans | declarative; manifestos, announcements, bold product statements |
| [capsule](design-presets/capsule.md) | pill shapes with ink outlines, cream, candy colors, Bodoni with a grotesk | friendly, warm; lifestyle and consumer brands, e-commerce |
| [cartesian](design-presets/cartesian.md) | warm stone palette, taupe hairline grid, Playfair with Inter, drafted rings | quiet, literary; luxury, architecture, research |
| [cobalt-grid](design-presets/cobalt-grid.md) | cream paper, cobalt ink, permanent graph grid, serif with grotesk and mono | systematic, technical-editorial; developer tools, data, infrastructure |
| [code-editorial](design-presets/code-editorial.md) | warm cream, scarce terracotta, Garamond display, a navy code surface | considered, developer-facing; launches, changelogs and docs with code |
| [coral](design-presets/coral.md) | coral, ink and cream planes at hard edges, diagonal hatch, condensed display, giant numerals | bold magazine energy; product drops, list videos, fashion and sport |
| [creative-mode](design-presets/creative-mode.md) | cream, 4px ink borders, hard offset shadows, black heavy display, mono taxonomy | punchy but restrained; creator tools, studios, tutorials with attitude |
| [daisy-days](design-presets/daisy-days.md) | sunny pastels, charcoal outlines, rounded friendly type, hand-drawn ornaments | playful, warm; education, kids, cafés, gifts |
| [editorial-forest](design-presets/editorial-forest.md) | green, pink and cream, a serif display, mono chrome, 2px hairlines, monogram stamp | spacious, literary calm; wellness, sustainability, publishing |

Pick by the brand's temperament first, then check the fit. Use one preset per
video. When a frame needs a component the preset lacks, borrow it from another
preset and restyle it in this preset's tokens.

## Video-type rules

These sit on top of whichever preset is chosen.

- **Product demo (app, SaaS, tool)**: real screens at 45–70% of the frame width.
  Mark a region on the full screen before pushing into it (scale 1.6–2.0 over
  0.8–1.2s). A 40px cursor with a click ring; typed input at 2–4 characters per
  0.1s. Change the screen's state every 1–2s and carry the same screen across
  scenes instead of cutting to new layouts.
- **Physical product or offer**: supplied product images only; the product is
  the largest element in hero frames (50–75% of the height). At most three
  callouts with leader lines per view. One offer element per frame; only the
  closing frame pairs the price with the CTA. Never invent prices, discounts,
  ratings or sales counts.
- **Short-form 9:16**: essential text between y=220 and y=1540 and left of x=940.
  The hook and a visual of its payoff are readable at frame 0. At most 12 CJK
  characters or 6 English words a line, three lines a frame. Cut every 1–2
  beats; captions sit above y=1540.
- **Tutorial or how-to**: one action per step frame, each on the real UI. Mark
  the control with an outline, dim the rest, then push in. At most five numbered
  pins per screen. Menu names, button labels and shortcuts exactly as in the product.
- **Numbers and reports**: one number per frame carries the accent. Every chart
  frame shows its unit and source; bar axes start at zero. Count-ups take
  0.8–1.5s, except the cover, which shows the final figure at frame 0. Hold a
  finished chart 1.5s or more.
- **Brand film or teaser**: one line per frame; plates get a vignette and scale
  slowly (1.00→1.08 over the shot); cut to black for half a beat before the
  lockup.
- **A cast of people, agents or products**: one item per beat on hard cuts
  (0.5s at 120 BPM), then a summary frame listing all of them.

## Remap onto the brand

Every preset names color roles in its tokens. Map the brand onto them by role
and keep the structure:

- `canvas` → the brand's background; `ink` → its text color; `accent` → its
  primary; `deep` → its dark or ink; `surface` and `line` follow canvas and ink.
- A brand with one color keeps the preset's neutrals and puts that color on
  `accent`. Keep the preset's rule for how much of the frame `accent` may cover.
- If the brand primary fails contrast where the preset puts accent text, keep
  it for fields and marks, and set that text in `ink`.
- Fonts: use the brand's faces when they are installed or supplied, then the
  preset's named face, then its stack. Copy any font file the video depends on
  into `assets/fonts/` and load it with `@font-face`; never load a remote font.

## Fixed and free

- Fixed: the color-role rules, type roles and ramp, component shapes, frame-type
  grammar, motion vocabulary and the don'ts.
- Free: every word, number and image; which frame types appear, in what order
  and how often; which components a frame uses.

## Units and ratios

Sizes are px on a 1920×1080 frame. On 1080×1920 keep body, label and caption
sizes, and scale display sizes by 0.7–0.8 so the longest line fits about 920px.
On 1080×1080 scale display by about 0.8.

## Font stacks

Put the Latin face before the CJK face so mixed lines take each script's own
face. These stacks resolve on macOS and Windows without downloads.

- `serif-display`: "Didot", "Bodoni 72", "Bodoni MT", Georgia, then `song`
- `serif-text`: "Iowan Old Style", "Charter", Georgia, "Cambria", then `song`
- `sans`: "Avenir Next", "Helvetica Neue", "Segoe UI", Arial, then `hei`
- `condensed`: "Avenir Next Condensed", "DIN Condensed", "Bahnschrift", Impact, then `hei`
- `mono`: "SF Mono", Menlo, "Cascadia Mono", Consolas, monospace
- `song`: "Songti SC", "STSong", "Source Han Serif SC", "Noto Serif CJK SC", SimSun, serif
- `hei`: "PingFang SC", "Hiragino Sans GB", "Source Han Sans SC", "Noto Sans CJK SC", "Microsoft YaHei", sans-serif

PingFang SC stops at weight 600 and SimSun has one thin weight. When a preset
asks for heavier CJK than the machine has, raise size rather than fake bold, and
check the inspect frame.

## Rules every preset keeps

- Type floor: nothing on screen below 22px; body copy at least 28px.
- Casing: keep the approved copy's casing. Presets describe letter-spacing, never
  `text-transform: uppercase`.
- Frame 0: the cover's headline and hero are visible on the first frame; build
  the resolved frame first, then animate supporting parts into it.
- Real material first: product screens and photos come from `assets/product/`,
  supplied media or the reference. Never redraw a screen that was captured.
- Numbers: every figure, price, rating, date and count comes from the brief or a
  source. Ordinals such as 01, 02 are decoration and may be free.
- Local only: no remote fonts, scripts or images at render time.

# biennale-yellow — art-catalogue editorial

Adapted from the HyperFrames frame preset `biennale-yellow` (heygen-com/hyperframes,
Apache-2.0, see `LICENSE-hyperframes.txt`). Changed for Orkas VideoStudio: local
font stacks with CJK faces, px sizes with the 22px floor, approved-copy casing,
and a motion section.

Pick it when the brand wants museum-catalogue elegance and editorial authority:
confident, atmospheric, restrained. Launches told as an issue or exhibition,
founder stories, culture and design brands.
Failure looks like a flat CMS template (paper with no bloom) or a deck of
bordered cards.

## Tokens

```yaml
colors:             # keep the roles; remap by role (see design-presets.md)
  paper: "#E9E5DB"      # canvas: warm parchment on every frame
  paper-deep: "#DCD6C4" # canvas variant
  sun: "#F1EE2E"        # accent: bloom core, panel, tile underprint
  sun-soft: "#F8F39B"   # bloom middle stop
  haze: "#F0DA7C"       # bloom outer stop
  ink: "#1B2566"        # every line of type and every rule
  ember: "#E26B4A"      # counter-bloom only, 15–22%; never a fill or text
type:                # px on 1920×1080
  numeral-jumbo: { face: "Instrument Serif" > serif-display, size: 538, weight: 400, line: 0.84, tracking: -0.04em }
  display:       { face: "Instrument Serif" > serif-display, size: 280, weight: 400, line: 0.86, tracking: -0.018em }
  numeral-md:    { face: "Instrument Serif" > serif-display, size: 144, weight: 400, line: 0.92 }
  display-it:    { face: "Instrument Serif" > serif-display, size: 134, style: italic, line: 1.04 }
  date-rail:     { face: "Instrument Serif" > serif-display, size: 96, line: 0.96 }
  headline:      { face: "Instrument Serif" > serif-display, size: 88, line: 1.06 }
  headline-sm:   { face: "Instrument Serif" > serif-display, size: 64, line: 1.0 }
  strand-title:  { face: "Instrument Serif" > serif-display, size: 36, line: 1.1 }
  body:          { face: "Archivo" > sans, size: 32, weight: 400, line: 1.5 }
  body-lede:     { face: "Archivo" > sans, size: 36, weight: 400, line: 1.5 }
  label:         { face: "Archivo" > sans, size: 22, weight: 600, tracking: 0.18em }
  data:          { face: "JetBrains Mono" > mono, size: 24, tracking: 0.04em }
  pagenum:       { face: "JetBrains Mono" > mono, size: 22, opacity: 0.75 }
  cjk:           { display: song 700, body: hei 400 }
space: { edge: 80, region: 80, gap: 48, rule: 1 }
```

Faces: use the named face when installed or vendored in `assets/fonts/`,
otherwise the stack after `>`. Serif display stays weight 400; contrast comes
from size, never bold.

## Frame craft

- Squint: one serif moment dominates at 3–6× its neighbor; the sun bloom pulls
  the eye to it.
- Silence: frames stay 55–60% empty. The ledger is the one dense frame, dense
  through quiet hairline repetition.
- Restraint: one ink for all type and rules, one sun bloom per frame plus an
  optional ember counter-bloom. Never yellow type on ink.

## Components

- **sun-bloom**: a layered radial — sun at 70–95% core → sun-soft → haze at
  18–22% → paper at 0% — 42–70% of the frame, off-center or behind the focal
  element. One per frame; flat parchment reads as broken.
- **ember-bloom**: a radial in ember at 15–22% in the corner opposite the sun
  bloom; always subordinate.
- **block-tile**: sun rectangles at 40–70% opacity on an 8×4 grid behind cover
  and closing frames; a poster underprint.
- **yellow-panel**: a full-bleed sun column or third with ink type on it, meeting
  the paper directly with no border. The strongest color statement.
- **hairline-rule**: 1px ink; a soft variant at 18–20% for dense rows. The only
  border; nothing thicker exists.
- **strand-row**: serif numeral + serif title + sans body, soft hairline under.
  Numbered editorial lists.
- **ledger-row**: four columns — mono date · serif title · sans venue · mono
  duration on the right — with soft hairlines.
- **footer-band**: a four-column metadata strip at the foot of cover and closing
  frames, 1px ink rule over each cell.
- **vertical-rail**: a label rotated up the left edge as a section marker.
- **pagenum**: bottom-right, the only persistent chrome.

## Frame types

1. **Cover** — paper, a large sun bloom left of center, an ember bloom in the
   opposite corner. A two-line display headline left under a label, a date-rail
   top-right, a footer-band at the foot. Low density; readable at frame 0.
2. **Chapter divider** — a corner sun bloom, one numeral-jumbo dominating, a
   headline-sm title under it, a vertical-rail label up the left edge.
3. **Ledger** — headline-sm with a label top bar, then ledger rows under a 1px
   header rule. The dense frame; no accent, no bloom or a faint one.
4. **Manifesto** — a centered bloom, an oversized serif quote mark, a two-line
   display-it quote centered, a label attribution. About 60% open.
5. **Poster panel** — a yellow-panel column or third with a headline in ink on
   it; the paper side stays open.
6. **Strand list** — label, headline-sm, then numbered strand rows breathing
   under a subtle bloom.

## Motion

- Verbs: blooms breathe, lines rise into masks, hairlines draw, numerals swap,
  panels wipe across.
- Blooms scale 1→1.05 and drift 2–3% across the scene, `sine.inOut`; the
  atmosphere moves, the type holds.
- Display and headline lines reveal by a baseline mask, 0.6–0.8s `power3.out`,
  one line per beat.
- Hairlines draw left to right in 0.5s; ledger and strand rows follow them in
  sequence 0.12s apart.
- Chapter dividers cut on the downbeat; the numeral swaps with a hard cut.
- A yellow-panel enters as a wipe from its own edge in 0.5s `power2.inOut`.
- Never: bounce, rotation, shadows appearing, fast zooms on type.

## Do and don't

- Do start every frame on parchment with one sun bloom.
- Do set every line in ink; serif 400 display, sans body, mono for numerals and dates.
- Do lean sparse: left or asymmetric on cover, chapter and lists; centered only
  on the manifesto.
- Don't use drop shadows, rounded corners, bordered cards or rules thicker than 1px.
- Don't add a second text color, bold serif or inverted ink grounds.
- Don't run a headline edge to edge; step down the ramp instead.

## 9:16 and 1:1

- Cover: display at the top, footer-band stacks; 1:1 puts display in the upper half.
- Chapter divider: numeral centered, the rail moves to the top.
- Ledger: drop the venue column to three columns on 9:16 and 1:1.
- Poster panel: a top or bottom band on 9:16, a third on 1:1.

## Self-check before snapshot

- One serif display moment dominates; one sun bloom present; sparse frames 55–60% open.
- Ink for all text and rules; sun only as bloom, panel or tile; ember only as a counter-bloom.
- No shadow, no rounded corner, hairlines 1px.
- Copy keeps its approved casing; nothing below 22px.
- Every numeral and date traces to the brief; ordinals may be decorative.

# blockframe — candy neobrutalist blocks

Adapted from the HyperFrames frame preset `blockframe` (heygen-com/hyperframes,
Apache-2.0, see `LICENSE-hyperframes.txt`). Changed for Orkas VideoStudio: local
font stacks with CJK faces, px sizes with the 22px floor, approved-copy casing,
and a motion section.

Pick it when the product wants to feel confident and graphic: bold, punchy,
playful-loud. Consumer apps, creator tools, launches with a sense of humor,
anything that should feel like a sticker book or a toy box, not a deck.
Failure looks like a flat web card grid: thin or missing borders, blurred
shadows, everything politely aligned.

## Tokens

```yaml
colors:             # keep the roles; remap by role (see design-presets.md)
  black: "#000000"      # ink, line, deep: all type, every border and shadow, close ground
  white: "#FFFFFF"      # surface: card fills; border and type on the close-frame
  offwhite: "#FFFDF5"   # canvas: default ground
  pink: "#FE90E8"       # accent: pastel ground, icon square, star
  blue: "#C0F7FE"       # accent: pastel ground, icon square
  green: "#99E885"      # accent: pastel ground, icon square
  yellow: "#F7CB46"     # accent: CTA fill and the close-frame shadow
  cream: "#FFDC8B"      # canvas variant: cover ground, warm pastel
borders: { primary: 8, thin: 6 }   # px, black; source 0.4 / 0.3cqw at 1920
shadows: { default: 16, small: 8, hover: 12, close-yellow: 24, close-white: 12 }
type:                # px on 1920×1080
  heading-xl:  { face: "Inter" > sans, size: 96, weight: 900, line: 0.95, tracking: -0.03em }
  close-title: { face: "Inter" > sans, size: 81, weight: 900, line: 0.95, tracking: -0.03em }
  heading-lg:  { face: "Inter" > sans, size: 63, weight: 800, line: 1.0, tracking: -0.02em }
  stat-number: { face: "Inter" > sans, size: 63, weight: 900, line: 1.0 }
  quote-text:  { face: "Inter" > sans, size: 52, weight: 900, line: 1.15, tracking: -0.02em }
  heading-md:  { face: "Inter" > sans, size: 40, weight: 700, line: 1.1, tracking: -0.01em }
  card-title:  { face: "Inter" > sans, size: 36, weight: 700, line: 1.2 }
  body:        { face: "Inter" > sans, size: 32, weight: 500, line: 1.6 }
  label:       { face: "Space Grotesk" > sans, size: 22, weight: 600, tracking: 0.08em }
  counter:     { face: "Space Grotesk" > sans, size: 22, weight: 700, tracking: 0.1em }
  cjk:         { display: hei 900, body: hei 500 }
space: { edge: 60, gap: 33 }
```

Faces: use the named face when installed or vendored in `assets/fonts/`,
otherwise the stack after `>`; labels share the sans stack and differ by
tracking and weight. The source leans on capitals; copy keeps its approved
casing (CJK has no case), so weight 800–900, tight tracking, borders and
decorations carry the voice. PingFang stops at 600: raise CJK size, never fake bold.

## Frame craft

- Squint: one display moment dominates at 3–6× its neighbor; cards read as one system.
- Silence: cover, quote and close keep air, held by decorations rather than
  content. The feature and stat grids are the dense frames.
- Restraint: border and shadow travel in pairs (8↔16 cards, 6↔8 chrome, all
  black; white only on the closer); one pastel ground per frame, never a sixth.

## Components

- **card-elevated**: white, 8px black border, 16px hard shadow, square; the main card.
- **card-small**: white, 6px border, 8px shadow, square; stats, people, steps.
- **label-pill**: 6px border, 8px shadow, 9999px radius, pastel fill; opens every region.
- **button-primary**: yellow, black Inter 700, 6px border, 8px shadow, square.
- **star-burst**: a ten-point clip-path star, pastel, 6px border; corner attention.
- **stripe-block**: 45° stripes of black and one pastel inside a 6px border.
- **bg-dot-grid**: faint black dots, 2–3px on a 48px grid, over a corner or ground.
- **tilt-deco**: a block, badge or star turned 2–12°; stat cards alternate −2°/+2°.
- **stat-deco-dot**: a 24px pastel circle, 4px border, on stat cards; the only round shape.
- **close-frame**: black, white type, 8px white border, 24px yellow shadow; the closer.

## Frame types

1. **Cover** — cream or offwhite with a faint dot grid. A label-pill over a two-
   or three-line heading-xl on the left; tilted pastel blocks and a star break
   into the right third; a counter pill. Comfortable; readable at frame 0.
2. **Feature cards** — blue. Label-pill and heading-lg over three card-elevated
   cards, each a pastel icon square, card-title and body. Dense by design.
3. **Stat grid** — green. Three card-small stats tilted −2/+2°, each a deco dot,
   stat-number and label, under label-pill and heading-lg. Dense.
4. **Closing plate** — black. A white close-title inside the close-frame under
   an inverted label-pill; a pink star over one corner. About 50% open.
5. **Quote** — pink or offwhite. Quote-text in a card-elevated, label-pill
   above, attribution below, one decoration. Comfortable.
6. **Timeline** — offwhite. Three or four pastel card-small steps with step
   numbers, joined by black connector bars. Standard density.

## Motion

- Verbs: cards slam down, shadows snap out, pills and stars pop, tilts settle,
  grounds hard-cut.
- Cards slam in from 1.08× with a 24px shadow to rest in 0.3s `power4.out`;
  grids land one card per half-beat (0.25s at 120 BPM) in reading order.
- Pills, stars and deco dots pop from 0 in 0.35s `back.out(2)`; stat cards
  settle into their tilt in 0.4s `back.out(1.6)`.
- Press for emphasis: a card or the CTA moves 4px down-right as its shadow
  shrinks 4px (the hover token), 0.2s `power2.out`, back on the next beat.
- Chapters hard-cut on the downbeat to a new pastel with the headline set; the
  rest lands on the following beats.
- The cover's heading-xl and main decorations hold from frame 0.
- Never: crossfades, blurred or soft shadows, a shadow without its border,
  tweened border widths, rotation past 12°.

## Do and don't

- Do pair every border with its shadow: 8px with 16px, 6px with 8px.
- Do change the pastel ground every frame; the cycle is the rhythm.
- Do open each region with a label-pill and add one decoration per frame.
- Do keep shadows solid black, zero blur, bottom-right; yellow for the CTA.
- Do set display at 800–900, tracked tight; each line keeps its approved casing.
- Do fit the headline: up to 3 words heading-xl, 4–6 heading-lg, 7 or more
  heading-md, under 1500px wide. Lean most frames left.
- Don't round a corner except the deco dot, or blur any shadow.
- Don't color a border (white only on the closer) or add a sixth pastel.
- Don't set display untracked or a label as bare text.
- Don't align everything perfectly or leave a corner empty.

## 9:16 and 1:1

- Cover: title on top, decorations below; fewer decorations on 1:1.
- Feature cards: three stacked on 9:16; two plus one on 1:1.
- Stat grid: three tilted cards stacked on 9:16; 2×2 on 1:1.
- Closing and quote: centered; taller close-frame and stacked quote on 9:16.
- Timeline: vertical with connectors hidden on 9:16; 2×2 on 1:1.
- Drop decorations as the frame tightens: bordered, not cluttered.

## Self-check before snapshot

- One display moment dominates; the cards read as one system.
- Only the feature and stat grids run dense; cover, quote and close keep air.
- Every border has its shadow partner; solid black, zero blur, bottom-right.
- New pastel each frame; a label-pill and a decoration on each; square corners.
- Copy keeps its approved casing; nothing below 22px.
- Every figure, name and logo traces to the brief; otherwise leave it out.
  Counters and step numbers may be decorative.

# blue-professional — cream and cobalt briefing

Adapted from the HyperFrames frame preset `blue-professional` (heygen-com/hyperframes,
Apache-2.0, see `LICENSE-hyperframes.txt`). Changed for Orkas VideoStudio: local
font stacks with CJK faces, px sizes with the 22px floor, approved-copy casing,
and a motion section.

Pick it when the brand wants investment-research rigor and refined restraint:
measured, executive-readable, premium. B2B, finance, analytics, board updates.
Failure looks like a heavy-outlined, multi-color dashboard or cobalt headlines.

## Tokens

```yaml
colors:             # keep the roles; remap by role (see design-presets.md)
  bg: "#fdfae7"                         # canvas: warm cream on every frame
  primary: "#1e2bfa"                    # accent: the only one; eyebrows, figures, CTA, bars
  text: "#111111"                       # ink: headlines and quotes, never cobalt
  text-muted: "#6b6b6b"                 # ink-muted: body
  text-light: "#9a9a9a"                 # ink-light: tertiary chrome
  accent-light: "rgba(30,43,250,0.08)"  # accent tint: tag pills, bar tracks, highlight
  accent-medium: "rgba(30,43,250,0.15)" # accent tint, stronger: atmosphere
  border: "rgba(30,43,250,0.2)"         # line: card borders
  card-bg: "rgba(30,43,250,0.04)"       # surface: card fill
  positive: "#059669"                   # signal: upward change, text only
  negative: "#dc2626"                   # signal: downward change, text only
radii: { pill: 100, card-lg: 14, card-md: 12, card-sm: 10, bar: 6, circle: 50% }
type:                # px on 1920×1080; headings and quotes in text, figures in primary
  quote-mark:   { face: "Space Grotesk" > sans, size: 154, weight: 700, line: 0.5, color: primary, opacity: 0.15 }
  h1:           { face: "Space Grotesk" > sans, size: 81, weight: 700, line: 1.08, tracking: -0.02em }
  metric-value: { face: "Space Grotesk" > sans, size: 58, weight: 700, line: 1.0, color: primary }
  h2:           { face: "Space Grotesk" > sans, size: 50, weight: 600, line: 1.1, tracking: -0.02em }
  blockquote:   { face: "Space Grotesk" > sans, size: 46, weight: 500, line: 1.35 }
  h3:           { face: "Space Grotesk" > sans, size: 40, weight: 500, line: 1.3, tracking: -0.02em }
  stat-num:     { face: "Space Grotesk" > sans, size: 36, weight: 700, line: 1.0, color: primary }
  body:         { face: "Inter" > sans, size: 32, weight: 400, line: 1.6, color: text-muted }
  h4-eyebrow:   { face: "Space Grotesk" > sans, size: 22, weight: 600, tracking: 0.08em, color: primary }
  tag:          { face: "Space Grotesk" > sans, size: 22, weight: 500, color: primary }
  counter:      { face: "Space Grotesk" > sans, size: 22, weight: 500, tracking: 0.05em, color: text-muted }
  cjk:          { display: hei 600, body: hei 400 }
space: { edge: 96, top: 96, gap: 27 }
```

Faces: use the named face when installed or vendored in `assets/fonts/`,
otherwise the stack after `>`. Both faces fall back to one sans stack, so the
pair rests on weight and color: headings 500–700 near-black, body 400 gray. The
source sets eyebrows in tracked capitals; copy keeps its approved casing (CJK
has no case), so cobalt, weight 600, 0.08em and the accent-line carry them.

## Frame craft

- Squint: one near-black headline or cobalt figure dominates at 3–6× its neighbor.
- Silence: content frames read balanced, never crowded; the dashboard is the dense one.
- Restraint: cobalt carries every accent and nothing else does; headlines stay
  near-black; cards lift by tint, never shadow; green and red are inline text only.

## Components

- **card-tinted**: card-bg fill, 1.5px `border` line, 14px radius, no shadow; never solid.
- **metric-card**: the same shell with a cobalt metric-value, a label in text, a
  muted note, and an optional ↑/↓ chip in positive or negative text, no fill.
- **tag-pill**: accent-light fill, cobalt tag type, 100px radius; slide-header right.
- **cta-button**: a solid cobalt pill, cream Space Grotesk 600; the one solid element.
- **accent-line**: a 60×4px cobalt bar, 2px radius, above titles and under eyebrows.
- **bar-track**: a 28px accent-light track, 6px radius; the fill's width is the value.
- **step-circle**: 56px cobalt, cream numeral; steps fade 1.0 → 0.85 → 0.7 → 0.55.
- **split-highlight**: accent-light, 4px cobalt left rule, 12px radius; a pull quote.
- **slide-header**: cobalt eyebrow left, tag-pill right, h2 below; tops content frames.
- **atmosphere**: a clipped diagonal tint panel, a 3×3 cobalt dot grid, concentric
  rings. Cover and closing only.
- **progress-bar**: a 3px cobalt strip on the bottom edge; width grows by chapter.

## Frame types

1. **Cover** — cream, the diagonal tint panel over the right ~36%, a 3×3 dot
   grid. A two-line near-black h1 on the left under an accent-line and meta
   eyebrow, a muted body line below. Low density; readable at frame 0.
2. **Dashboard** — slide-header and h2 over three metric-cards: cobalt figure,
   label, muted note, optional chip. The dense frame; figures are the accent.
3. **Bar ranking** — eyebrow and h2 over three to five labeled bar-tracks with
   cobalt fills and percentages. Standard density.
4. **Pull quote** — centered over faint rings: a near-black blockquote under the
   15% cobalt quote-mark, a muted cite in the eyebrow style. About 55% open.
5. **Split + highlight** — an Inter body column beside a split-highlight pull
   quote, eyebrow and h2 above, a generous gutter. Standard.
6. **Closing / CTA** — cream with rings: accent-line, a centered near-black h1, a
   body line, the single cobalt cta-button below. About 60% open.

## Motion

- Verbs: masks lift lines, the accent-line draws, bars fill, cards fade up, rings drift.
- Headlines reveal by a baseline mask, 0.6s `power3.out`, one line per beat (0.5s
  at 120 BPM), after the accent-line draws 0→60px in 0.4s `power2.out`.
- Cards fade up 16px in 0.5s `power2.out`, 0.12s apart; a metric-value counts to
  the brief's figure in 0.8s `power1.out` and holds.
- Bars fill from the left in 0.7s `power3.out`, one per half-beat in rank order.
- The diagonal panel drifts about 2% and the rings breathe 1→1.04, `sine.inOut`.
- Chapters cut on the downbeat or push left in 0.6s `power2.inOut`; the
  slide-header lands first and the progress bar extends in 0.5s. The CTA may
  take a soft cobalt glow on its last beat, the only shadow the system allows.
- Never: bounce, elastic, rotation, a second color, card shadows, fast zooms on type.

## Do and don't

- Do start every frame on cream and let cobalt carry every accent.
- Do set headlines near-black at −0.02em, eyebrows cobalt at 0.08em, figures
  cobalt 600–700, body Inter 400 muted at 1.6; each line keeps its approved casing.
- Do use tinted cards (4% fill, 20% border, 10–14px radius, no shadow) and pill
  chrome; keep atmosphere and the one solid CTA for cover and closing.
- Do fit the headline: up to 3 words h1, 4–6 h2, 7 or more h3, under 1500px.
  Lean left on cover, dashboard and split; center quote and closer.
- Don't add a second accent or set a headline in cobalt.
- Don't shadow content, outline in opaque cobalt or square a content corner.
- Don't use the green and red chips as decoration; they mark a real comparison.
- Don't thicken borders to fill space, or run a headline edge to edge.

## 9:16 and 1:1

- Cover: title on top, the diagonal panel as a band below on 9:16; title in the
  upper half, dots in a corner on 1:1.
- Dashboard: three cards stacked on 9:16; 2×2 on 1:1.

- Cobalt is the only accent; headlines near-black; green and red inline only.
- Cards tinted and rounded, 20% borders, no shadow; atmosphere on cover and closing.
- Left on cover, dashboard and split; centered on quote and closer.

# bold-poster — tilted red editorial poster

Adapted from the HyperFrames frame preset `bold-poster` (heygen-com/hyperframes,
Apache-2.0, see `LICENSE-hyperframes.txt`). Changed for Orkas VideoStudio: local
font stacks with CJK faces, px sizes with the 22px floor, approved-copy casing,

Pick it when the brand wants editorial authority and vintage gravitas: powerful,
printed, restrained. Results told loud, sports, food and culture brands, campaigns.
Failure looks like a rounded, soft-shadowed, multi-accent slide, or a straight hero.

## Tokens

```yaml
colors:             # keep the roles; remap by role (see design-presets.md)
  bg: "#FFFFFF"     # canvas: the white sheet; type on red and dark panels
  dark: "#1C1410"   # ink, line, deep: body, headers, grid rules, dark panel
  red: "#D8000F"    # accent: figures, rules, labels, leftbars, bullets, progress, red panel
  light: "#F5F2EF"  # surface: off-white alternating stripes and panels

  stat-big:          { face: "Shrikhand" > serif-display, size: 422, weight: 400, line: 0.82, color: red, rotate: -6deg }
  hero-title-red:    { face: "Shrikhand" > serif-display, size: 259, weight: 400, line: 0.85, color: red, rotate: -4deg }
  close-big:         { face: "Shrikhand" > serif-display, size: 259, weight: 400, line: 0.88, color: red, rotate: -5deg }
  hero-title:        { face: "Shrikhand" > serif-display, size: 221, weight: 400, line: 0.88 }
  hero-title-bottom: { face: "Shrikhand" > serif-display, size: 200, weight: 400, line: 0.9, rotate: 2deg }
  red-quote:         { face: "Shrikhand" > serif-display, size: 90, weight: 400, line: 1.15, color: bg, shadow: stacked }
  section-header:    { face: "Shrikhand" > serif-display, size: 63, weight: 400, line: 1.0 }
  cell-number:       { face: "Shrikhand" > serif-display, size: 52, weight: 400, line: 1.0, color: red }
  card-title:        { face: "Shrikhand" > serif-display, size: 36, weight: 400, line: 1.1 }
  body:              { face: "Libre Baskerville" > serif-text, size: 32, weight: 400, line: 1.75 }
  body-cell:         { face: "Libre Baskerville" > serif-text, size: 32, weight: 400, line: 1.55 }
  bullet-body:       { face: "Space Grotesk" > mono, size: 32, weight: 400, line: 1.45 }
  label:             { face: "Space Grotesk" > mono, size: 22, weight: 600, tracking: 0.2em, color: red }
  cjk:               { display: song 900, body: song 400, label: hei 600 }
space: { edge-y: 58, edge-x: 69, gap-y: 29, gap-x: 38 }
```

Faces: use the named face when installed or vendored in `assets/fonts/`,
otherwise the stack after `>`. Shrikhand has no local look-alike: vendor it (OFL);
if the stack takes over, set display at 700 so a Bodoni or Didot bold keeps the
weight. Space Grotesk is chrome on the mono stack; bold in body switches to it at
600. The source sets labels in tracked capitals; copy keeps its approved casing (CJK
has no case), so red, 600 and 0.2em carry them, and tilt and red carry CJK display.

## Frame craft

- Squint: one display moment (hero stack, stat-big or close-big) dominates at 3–6×.
- Silence: statement frames hold 50–60% empty; the financial grid is the dense one.
- Restraint: four colors, red the only accent; one display moment per frame; the
  stacked text-shadow on red display is the only shadow; three bullets at most.

## Components

- **hero-title-stack**: three Shrikhand lines (hero-title, -red, -bottom), at least
  one red and one tilted, −4° or +2°; the signature opener.
- **stat-big**: the poster numeral at −6°, red on white or white on red with the shadow.
- **fin-grid**: 3px dark outer border, 1.5px dark inner rules meeting at every
  crossing, square; cells hold a red cell-number, a label and body-cell text.
- **red-leftbar-card**: no outline, no shadow, square; a 4px red left rule, 19px of
  padding, then card-title, body and bullets.
- **red-panel** / **dark-panel**: full-bleed red or dark with white type; red accents
  on dark, the stacked shadow on display set on red.
- **stacked-text-shadow**: `2px 2px 0 rgba(28,20,16,.25), 4px 4px 0 rgba(28,20,16,.2),
  6px 6px 0 rgba(28,20,16,.15)`; a text-shadow, on the red panel only.
- **bullet**: a red em-dash or round glyph hung at the left edge; no disc; three max.
- **progress-bar**: a 10px red strip on the bottom edge, width growing by chapter.

## Frame types

1. **Hero stack** — white. The hero-title-stack on the left, a mono label above,
   a Baskerville tagline below, progress bar and counter at the foot; the right
   half open. Readable at frame 0.
2. **Hero stat** — full red. A white stat-big at −6° with the stacked shadow,
   centered, a label above, a Baskerville line below. About 60% open.
3. **Financial grid** — white, tight padding. Label and section-header over the
   fin-grid: red numerals, mono labels, serif body. The dense frame.
4. **Pull quote** — full red. A two-line white red-quote with the stacked shadow,
   left, a Baskerville cite beneath. About 50% open.
5. **Editorial cards** — white or off-white stripes. Two or three
   red-leftbar-cards under label and section-header. Standard density.
6. **Closing statement** — white or dark. A red close-big at −5°, a label and a
   Baskerville contact line, progress bar at the foot. About 60% open.

## Motion

- Verbs: panels hard-cut, display slams in at its tilt, rules draw, cells snap in.
- Statement display slams from 1.15× to rest in 0.3s `power4.out` on the downbeat;
  its tilt is set from the first frame and never spins in.
- The hero stack is resolved at frame 0; label, tagline and progress bar arrive
  around it, one per half-beat (0.25s at 120 BPM).
- Red and dark panels arrive as hard cuts on the downbeat; the stacked shadow is
  on from the panel's first frame and never animates.
- Fin-grid: the outer border draws in 0.5s `power2.inOut`, inner rules 0.2s
  behind; cells fill row by row on half-beats, numerals cut in whole.
- Leftbar rules grow downward in 0.4s `power3.out` before their text; bullets
  tick in 0.25s apart. The progress bar steps at each cut in 0.2s `power2.out`.
- Never: crossfaded panels, blur, bouncing type, a tilt rotating into place, two
  display moves in one frame.

## Do and don't

- Do stack the hero in three Shrikhand lines, at least one tilted and one red.
- Do set every figure in red Shrikhand; tilt statement display −5° to −6°.
- Do set labels in mono 600 at 0.2em in red and body in Baskerville at 1.75;
  each line keeps its approved casing.
- Do rule data with the 3px + 1.5px double border, use leftbar cards elsewhere,
  and cap red em-dash bullets at three.
- Do fit the line: up to 2 words stat-big or hero-title-red, 3–4 hero-title, 5 or
  more section-header, under 1500px; one display moment per frame.
- Don't add a second accent, round a corner, or use any other shadow.
- Don't put Shrikhand in body, serif in labels or the label face in headlines.
- Don't use disc bullets, leave a red statement untilted, or crowd a statement frame.

## 9:16 and 1:1

- Hero stack: centered and taller on 9:16; stack over tagline on 1:1.
- Hero stat and closing: centered; close-big stacks on 9:16.
- Financial grid: two across or stacked on 9:16; 2×2 on 1:1.
- Pull quote: stacked on 9:16, centered on 1:1; editorial cards stack on both.
- Tilts hold on every ratio without clipping; the progress bar spans the bottom.

## Self-check before snapshot

- One display moment dominates; statement frames 50–60% open; only the fin-grid is dense.
- Four colors; red the lone accent and never body text.
- Statements tilted, figures red, no tilted line clipped; Baskerville body at 1.75.
- Flat: the stacked text-shadow on red display is the only shadow; square
  corners; three bullets at most.
- Copy keeps its approved casing; nothing below 22px.
- Every figure, name and logo traces to the brief; otherwise leave it out.
  Counters and progress are decorative.

# broadside — two-register protest poster

Adapted from the HyperFrames frame preset `broadside` (heygen-com/hyperframes,
Apache-2.0, see `LICENSE-hyperframes.txt`). Changed for Orkas VideoStudio: local
font stacks with CJK faces, px sizes with the 22px floor, approved-copy casing,
and a motion section.

Pick it when the brand wants presence and authority carried by type alone: bold,
typographic, declarative. Manifestos, positioning, design-led and developer brands.

## Tokens

```yaml
colors:             # keep the roles; remap by role (see design-presets.md)
  ink-black: "#111111"                        # deep: dark-register ground; type on orange
  ink-black-alt: "#1A1A18"                    # deep variant
  fire-orange: "#E85D26"                      # accent: lone accent on dark; the orange register
  cream: "#F0ECE5"                            # ink on the dark register
  cream-muted: "#888880"                      # ink-muted on dark

  ink-on-orange-hint: "rgba(17,17,17,0.55)"   # ink-hint on orange: kicker
  ink-on-orange-faint: "rgba(17,17,17,0.40)"  # faint on orange: catalogue mark
```
