```yaml
  h1:             { face: "Barlow" > sans, size: 144, weight: 800, line: 0.9, tracking: -0.03em }
  fadelist-item:  { face: "Barlow" > sans, size: 144, weight: 900, line: 1.0, tracking: -0.03em }
  stat-value:     { face: "Barlow" > sans, size: 106, weight: 900, line: 1.0, tracking: -0.04em }
  h2:             { face: "Barlow" > sans, size: 86, weight: 700, line: 1.1, tracking: -0.02em }
  quote-text:     { face: "Barlow" > sans, size: 73, weight: 700, line: 1.15, tracking: -0.02em }
  h3:             { face: "Barlow" > sans, size: 54, weight: 600, line: 1.2 }
  lead:           { face: "Barlow" > sans, size: 36, weight: 400, line: 1.5 }
  body:           { face: "Barlow" > sans, size: 28, weight: 400, line: 1.6 }
  caption:        { face: "Barlow" > sans, size: 24, weight: 400, line: 1.5 }
  label:          { face: "IBM Plex Mono" > mono, size: 22, weight: 500, tracking: 0.14em }

```

Faces: use the named face when installed or vendored in `assets/fonts/`,
otherwise the stack after `>`. Barlow carries every text role, its range from
weight 400–900 and size; mono is chrome only. The source sets display lowercase
and chrome in capitals; copy keeps its approved casing. A lowercase brief line is
the native register; otherwise 900, size and tight tracking carry the look. CJK
has no case, so the registers carry it; PingFang stops at 600, so raise size.

## Frame craft

- Squint: one display moment dominates at 3–6×, big enough to read as shape first.
- Silence: declarative frames stay 45–55% empty; the stat grid is the dense one.
- Restraint: one register per frame; fire-orange is the only hue, accent on dark
  and environment on orange; three bullets at most.

## Components

- **registers**: two surfaces, one per frame. Dark: ink-black, cream type, orange
  accent. Orange: fire-orange, ink-black type, ink overlays for muted tones.
- **slide-chrome**: 1px bars top and bottom (border-dark, or 20% ink on orange),
  label left, number right; off on cover, chapter, statement, quote and end.
- **kicker**: the mono eyebrow, fire-orange on dark, 55% ink on orange.
- **rule**: a 36×2px stub, orange on dark, ink on orange; the only ornament.
- **broadside-num**: a faint mono catalogue numeral top-left on orange covers.
- **stat-card**: a single 1px border-dark top rule; stat-value, body and a label.
- **bullet**: a fire-orange mono `/` before each lead-size item; three at most.
- **bar-track**: vertical bars on a 1px left axis; cream-hint bars, one orange.
- **compare-panel**: two equal panels split by a 1px rule; the right may fill orange.
- **fadelist**: three fadelist-item words at opacity 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.22 facing one
  oversized fadelist-title.

## Frame types

1. **Cover** (orange) — a one- or two-word display in ink, left, over the rule
   stub and a kicker, a lead in 75% ink beneath; broadside-num top-left, meta
   top-right, no bars. About 45% open; readable at frame 0.
2. **Statement** (dark) — a two-to-four-word display or h1 in cream, left, one
   clause in fire-orange, a kicker, no bars. About 55% open.
3. **Stat grid** (dark, bars on) — a kicker over three stat-cards: orange 900
   figures, Barlow labels, mono notes. The dense frame.
4. **Fadelist** (dark) — the three-step word stack facing a fire-orange
   fadelist-title: before, during, after. Low to moderate density.
5. **Pull quote** (dark, bars off) — 700 quote-text under the oversized orange
   quote-mark, block under 1500px, a mono name and role. About 50% open.
6. **Compare** (dark into orange) — a dark panel documenting in cream beside an
   orange panel declaring in ink, a mono label and h3 on each. Standard.

## Motion

- Verbs: registers hard-cut, words slam, one clause ignites, hairlines draw.
- Register changes are hard cuts on the downbeat, never a crossfade; the cut is
  the punctuation.
- Display and h1 words land one per beat (0.5s at 120 BPM), 1.06× to rest in
  0.25s `power4.out`; the clause turns orange on its own beat, no color tween.
- Hairlines draw in 0.4s `power2.inOut`; each figure cuts in whole once its rule
  is down. Bars rise in 0.6s `power3.out`, the orange one last.
- Fadelist words arrive on successive beats already at their opacity; the title
  slams in last.
- On the cover the display word holds from frame 0; the rule stub draws, then
  kicker, lead and numeral arrive on half-beats.
- Never: shadows, blur, rotation, bounce, crossfaded registers, two display moves.

## Do and don't

- Do set Barlow display at 900, tracked tight; each line keeps its approved casing.
- Do make fire-orange the environment on declarative frames, the lone accent on dark.
- Do keep chrome in mono at 0.14em and mark bullets with the mono `/`, three at most.
- Do say one statement per frame; build hierarchy from weight, size and 1px rules.
- Do leave chrome bars off declarative frames; lean left; the type is the layout.
- Do fit the line: up to 2 words display, 3–4 h1, 5 or more h2, under 1500px.
- Don't add a second accent or a cream/paper register, or set cream type on orange.
- Don't use drop shadows, rounded surfaces or gradient grounds.
- Don't add a serif companion or set chrome in Barlow.

## 9:16 and 1:1

- Cover: word on top, lead below on 9:16; centered word on 1:1.
- Statement: stacked taller on 9:16, centered on 1:1. Fadelist: stack over title.
- Stat grid: three stacked on 9:16; two plus one on 1:1.
- Pull quote: mark on top, quote below on 9:16; centered on 1:1.
- Compare: dark over orange, stacked, on both. Mono chrome stays Latin and digits.

## Self-check before snapshot

- Exactly one display moment dominates; only the stat grid runs dense.
- Declarative frames 45–55% empty, chrome bars off.
- One register per frame; ink on orange, cream on dark; no second hue.
- No shadow, no radius, 1px hairlines; three bullets at most, each with the `/`.
- Copy keeps its approved casing; nothing below 22px.
- Every figure, name and logo traces to the brief; otherwise leave it out.
  Catalogue numerals may run in sequence.

# capsule — pill-shaped playful editorial

Adapted from the HyperFrames frame preset `capsule` (heygen-com/hyperframes,
Apache-2.0, see `LICENSE-hyperframes.txt`). Changed for Orkas VideoStudio: local
font stacks with CJK faces, px sizes with the 22px floor, approved-copy casing,
and a motion section.

Pick it when the brand wants to feel friendly, soft and approachable yet still
editorial: consumer apps, creator tools, community launches, playful explainers.
Failure looks like a flat SaaS card grid: unstroked boxes, no pills, bare corners.

## Tokens

```yaml
colors:             # keep the roles; remap by role (see design-presets.md)
  cream: "#F5F5F0"    # canvas: every frame, under glows and grain
  ink: "#1A1A1A"      # ink: every headline and line of body
  outline: "#1E1E1E"  # line: the stroke around every pill
  white: "#FFFFFF"    # surface: content pills and cards
  coral: "#E85D4E"    # accent, warm: accent-line, first card-icon
  lime: "#C4D94E"     # accent, bright neutral: orbit center, highlight
  lavender: "#C5B5E0" # accent, cool: header tag-pill
  sky: "#8BB4F7"      # accent, cool: highlight, card-icon
  violet: "#A06CE8"   # accent, cool: closing italic word
  yellow: "#F2D160"   # accent, warm: title-pill
  peach: "#F5B895"    # accent, warm
  mint: "#A8E6CF"     # accent, cool
  shadow: "rgba(26,26,26,0.08)" # deep: offset shadows only, 8% ink
type:                # px on 1920×1080
  display:          { face: "Bodoni Moda" > serif-display, size: 230, weight: 800, line: 0.88, tracking: -0.03em }
  closing-display:  { face: "Bodoni Moda" > serif-display, size: 163, weight: 800, line: 0.95, tracking: -0.03em }
  headline:         { face: "Bodoni Moda" > serif-display, size: 96, weight: 700, line: 1.05, tracking: -0.02em }
  quote-display:    { face: "Bodoni Moda" > serif-display, size: 81, weight: 600, line: 1.3, tracking: -0.01em }
  section-headline: { face: "Bodoni Moda" > serif-display, size: 77, weight: 700, line: 1.05, tracking: -0.01em }
  stat-number:      { face: "Bodoni Moda" > serif-display, size: 69, weight: 800, line: 1.0, tracking: -0.03em }
  orbit-numeral:    { face: "Bodoni Moda" > serif-display, size: 50, weight: 700, line: 1.0 }
  card-headline:    { face: "Bodoni Moda" > serif-display, size: 36, weight: 700, line: 1.1 }
  subtitle:         { face: "Space Grotesk" > sans, size: 36, weight: 400, tracking: 0.18em }
  body:             { face: "Space Grotesk" > sans, size: 32, weight: 400, line: 1.6 }
  pill-text:        { face: "Space Grotesk" > sans, size: 24, weight: 600, tracking: 0.12em }
  label:            { face: "Space Grotesk" > sans, size: 22, weight: 500, tracking: 0.1em }
  cjk:              { display: song 700, body: hei 400 }
space: { edge: 96, gap: 38, card-pad: [38, 31], stroke: 4, pill-radius: 9999, card-radius: 32 }
```

Faces: use the named face when installed or vendored in `assets/fonts/`,
otherwise the stack after `>`. Bodoni runs 700–800 (600 on quotes), always ink;
where the stack stops at bold, take its bold and never fake a heavier weight.

## Frame craft

- Squint: one Bodoni headline or stat dominates at 3–6× its nearest neighbor.
- Silence: declarative frames fill with atmosphere, not content; their pills are
  wallpaper. Pillar cards and the stat grid are the dense frames and drop it.
- Restraint: every pill stroked, candy on fills and stat numerals only, shadows
  under content only. The nine candies mean nothing: mix warm, cool and lime,
  never two of a family side by side. A brand primary takes one slot; no tenth.

## Components

- **pill**: the container for every chip, button, label, tile, node and bar:
  9999px radius small, 32px on cards, 4px outline, candy or white fill, never
  unstroked. Shadows fall down-right in `shadow`, unblurred: 4px on small nodes,
  6px on stat and title pills and satellites, 8px on cards, 12px on a screen.
- **pill-card**: white, 32px radius, outline, 8px shadow, padded 38/31; a
  card-icon, a card-headline, then body.
- **stat-pill**: white, 32px, outline, 6px shadow; a candy stat-number over a
  pill-text label and a 40px candy bar. The one place color touches a numeral.
- **title-pill**: a yellow 9999px pill, outline, 6px shadow, over the headline.
- **card-icon**: a 60px outlined candy circle holding an ink Bodoni numeral.
- **floating-pill**: outlined candy pills and dots tilted −20° to +25°, flat, 5–8
  per declarative frame, off the edges; short neutral words from the brief, or none.
- **quote-highlight**: an outlined lime or sky pill wrapped around one phrase of
  a Bodoni quote; it replaces bold.
- **bar-track**: a 36px outlined cream track filled by a candy pill, value at its end.
- **accent-line**: a coral pill rule, 60×4px (80×4 on the closing frame).
- **atmosphere**: 1–3 radial candy glows at 6–15% over cream, 4% grain; every frame.

## Frame types

1. **Cover** — glows, grain and 5–8 floating pills at the edges; a yellow
   title-pill over a one- or two-line display headline in ink, centered, a key
   word in candy italic; accent-line and subtitle beneath. Readable at frame 0.
2. **Pillar cards** — no wallpaper; a lavender tag-pill and section-headline over
   three pill-cards with coral, sky and lime icons. The dense frame.
3. **Stat grid** — a centered section-headline over a row of 3–4 stat-pills.
4. **Pull quote** — a few floating pills; a quote-display quote in ink at left,
   one phrase highlighted, accent-line, label attribution. About half open.
5. **Orbit** — a 160px lime circle with an orbit-numeral ordinal, circled by 4–6
   tilted candy satellites with 6px shadows.
6. **Closing plate** — wallpaper back; a yellow title-pill over a centered
   closing-display sign-off in ink, one word in violet italic, 80px accent-line.

## Motion

- Verbs: pills pop, shadows land, wallpaper floats, highlights sweep, bars fill.
- Content pills pop from scale 0.86 in 0.45s `back.out(1.7)`, 0.1s apart, so
  three cards land in one beat; each shadow slides out 0.1s later, in 0.2s.
- Floating pills are in place from the start and drift 8–16px with a 2–4° sway,
  `sine.inOut` yoyo; the glows breathe with them.
- Bodoni lines rise 24px from a baseline mask, 0.6s `power3.out`, a line per
  beat; a highlight sweeps under its phrase on the next beat in 0.4s.
- Bars grow from the left, 0.7s `power3.out`, while numerals count up to the
  brief's value; orbit satellites settle in on `back.out(1.4)`, 0.1s apart.
- Chapters cut on the downbeat, hard or behind one candy pill wiping across, 0.5s.
- Never: elastic wobble, spinning pills, blurred shadows, a headline that bounces.

## Do and don't

- Do make every container a stroked pill: 9999px small, 32px cards, 4px outline.
- Do set Bodoni in ink, negative-tracked; color only on stat numerals, pill fills
  and one italic key word. Shadows under content pills; floating pills flat.
- Do fill declarative frames with pills, glows and grain; center cover, closing
  and orbit, anchor cards and quote left.
- Don't use a sharp text box, an unstroked pill, a blurred or recolored shadow,
  bold for emphasis, a tenth candy, or a headline running edge to edge.
- Copy keeps its approved casing; pill text, labels and subtitle get their look
  from weight 500–600 and 0.1–0.18em tracking (CJK has no case).

## 9:16 and 1:1

- Cover: display on top, pills as a band below on 9:16; centered, fewer pills on 1:1.
- Pillar cards: three stacked on 9:16, two plus one on 1:1; stats 2×2 on both.
- Quote: on top with the highlight inline on 9:16; centered on 1:1. Closing: centered.
- Orbit: three satellites on 9:16, four on 1:1; fewer floating pills as it tightens.

## Self-check before snapshot

- One Bodoni element dominates at 3–6×; only pillar cards and stats run dense.
- Every container a stroked pill; candy on fills, stat numerals, one italic word.
- Shadows unblurred and under content only; glow and grain on every frame.
- Copy keeps its approved casing; nothing below 22px.
- Every figure, name and logo traces to the brief; otherwise leave it out.

```yaml
  display:           { face: "Playfair Display" > serif-display, size: 154, weight: 400, line: 1.04 }
  quote-mark:        { face: "Playfair Display" > serif-display, size: 173, weight: 400, line: 0.5, color: line }

  h3:                { face: "Playfair Display" > serif-display, size: 35, weight: 400, line: 1.1 }
  subtitle:          { face: "Inter" > sans, size: 36, weight: 400, line: 1.5 }

```

Faces: use the named face when installed or vendored in `assets/fonts/`,
otherwise the stack after `>`. Playfair stays weight 400 in ink, never bold or
taupe; contrast comes from size and the serif–sans switch. Italic on a key word.

## Frame craft

- Squint: one Playfair moment dominates at 3–6× its neighbor; serif against sans
  and size carry the hierarchy, never weight.
- Silence: declarative frames stay 55–60% empty. No frame is dense; even the
  agenda breathes, because crowding is what breaks this system.
- Restraint: two geo rings per frame at most, the one ink rule used sparingly, no
  attention color: five stones and ink. A brand accent stays at label scale.

## Components

- **hairline**: 1px solid `line`. Every separator, card edge, timeline rule and
  photo ring is this line; nothing thicker exists.
- **card**: white-overlay fill in a 1px line border, square, no shadow; the faint
  fill is what sets it apart from bare stone.
- **card-icon**: a 40px circle ringed in 1px line, a taupe Playfair numeral inside.
- **agenda-row**: taupe Playfair numeral left, ink Playfair label right, both h3,
  on a 1px line.
- **timeline**: one 1px line across the top of all phases; year, timeline-headline
  and body under it. No nodes, no dots.
- **stats-cluster**: modest stat-figures under a 1px top rule with taupe labels;
  never a hero numeral.
- **geo-ring**: a 1px line circle 192–960px across at 20–50% opacity, a dashed
  inner ring at 70–80% of its diameter; compass work behind content, 1–2 a frame.
- **horizontal-accent**: 346×1px in text-primary, the only ink line; cover and closing.
- **vertical-line**: optional 1px line at 30–40%, full height, ~96px in from an edge.
- **image-placeholder**: a bg-secondary plate in a 1px line border holding a
  supplied photo or screen; with none, a crossed X of 1px taupe diagonals at ±30°
  and a micro caption — a drafting mark, never a fake picture.
- **team-photo**: a bg-secondary circle ringed in 1px line with a supplied
  portrait or a taupe Playfair initial.

## Frame types

1. **Cover** — a 650px geo ring right of center, an optional vertical-line left; a
   taupe label over a two- or three-line display or h1 in ink at left, italic key
   word, then subtitle, optional meta row and ink rule. ~55% empty; readable at frame 0.
2. **Agenda / index** — a label and an h2 over 4–6 generously spaced agenda
   rows; taupe numerals are the only emphasis.
3. **Pull quote** — centered on a dashed 500px ring: the quote-mark at half
   opacity, a two-line quote at h2 in ink, a taupe attribution. About 60% open.
4. **Closing plate** — centered in the largest ring (~770px): a label, an h1 or
   display sign-off with an italic word, a horizontal-accent. About 60% open.
5. **Two-column editorial** — columns 115px apart: label, h2 and body on one side,
   an image-placeholder or card on the other. No accent.
6. **Stats / timeline** — a label and an h3 over a stats-cluster or a timeline,
   each under its 1px top rule. No accent, no nodes.

## Motion

- Verbs: rings draw, hairlines draw, lines rise into masks, labels fade, rings drift.
- A ring draws its circumference in 0.9s `power2.inOut`, the dashed inner ring
  0.25s behind, then turns 2–4° across the scene on `sine.inOut`.
- Headlines reveal by a baseline mask, 0.7s `power3.out`, a line per beat; the
  italic word arrives with its line. The cover headline is set from frame 0.
- Hairlines draw left to right in 0.6s `power2.out`; rows and phases follow 0.15s
  apart, fading up 12px. Labels fade in over 0.4s `sine.out` half a beat later.
- The horizontal-accent draws last, 0.5s `power2.inOut`, on a downbeat.
- Chapters change on the downbeat with a 0.4s crossfade; no wipes, no slides.
- Never: bounce, overshoot, scale pops, rotating type, shadows, fast zooms.

## Do and don't

- Do make every separator one 1px line; set Playfair at 400 in ink, body in
  text-secondary, labels in taupe with wide tracking.
- Do layer one or two geo rings behind content; fill plates with bg-secondary.
- Do let frames breathe, never crowded; center quote and closing, the rest left.
- Don't add an attention color, bold Playfair, set a headline in taupe, or draw a
  border of 2px or more.
- Don't add shadows, elevated cards or rounded rectangles; circles are the only
  curve. Don't run a headline edge to edge.
- Copy keeps its approved casing; labels get their look from taupe, size and
  0.13–0.21em tracking (CJK has no case).

## 9:16 and 1:1

- Cover: headline on top, ring below on 9:16; upper half, ring behind on 1:1.
- Quote and closing: centered, the ring scaled to the short side; agenda rows tighten.
- Two-column editorial: stacks, text over the plate, on both ratios.
- Stats / timeline: a vertical list without the top rule on 9:16; compact on 1:1.

## Self-check before snapshot

- One Playfair moment dominates; declarative frames 55–60% empty, none crowded.
- Five stones and ink; headlines ink, body gray, labels taupe; two rings at most.
- Every separator 1px; horizontal-accent the only ink rule; no shadow or rounded box.
- Copy keeps its approved casing; nothing below 22px.
- Every figure, name and logo traces to the brief; otherwise leave it out.

# cobalt-grid — two-color risograph on graph paper

Adapted from the HyperFrames frame preset `cobalt-grid` (heygen-com/hyperframes,
Apache-2.0, see `LICENSE-hyperframes.txt`). Changed for Orkas VideoStudio: local
font stacks with CJK faces, px sizes with the 22px floor, approved-copy casing,
and a motion section.

Pick it when the brand wants clarity and measured authority: restrained,
systemic, editorial. Trend reports, research and data stories, developer and
infrastructure brands, annual reviews.
Failure looks like a colorful dashboard with a second hue, or the grid switched off.

## Tokens

```yaml
colors:             # keep the roles; remap by role (see design-presets.md)
  paper: "#F0EBDE"                  # canvas: cream on every frame
  paper-2: "#E6E0CE"                # canvas variant; never a card
  ink: "#1F2BE0"                    # ink and accent: the only ink there is
  ink-soft: "#5560E5"               # ink-muted: italic callouts only
  grid: "rgba(31,43,224,0.10)"      # line: graph grid, chart off-cells
  ink-faint: "rgba(31,43,224,0.18)" # line, soft: ledger row dividers
type:                # px on 1920×1080
  vbig-numeral:    { face: "Newsreader" > serif-text, size: 240, weight: 400, line: 0.9, tracking: -0.015em }
  display-hero:    { face: "Newsreader" > serif-text, size: 200, weight: 400, line: 0.9, tracking: -0.008em }
  display-closing: { face: "Newsreader" > serif-text, size: 180, weight: 400, line: 0.96, tracking: -0.005em }
  display-chapter: { face: "Newsreader" > serif-text, size: 131, weight: 400, line: 1.0, tracking: -0.005em }
  display-quote:   { face: "Newsreader" > serif-text, size: 109, weight: 400, line: 1.05, tracking: -0.005em }
  headline-index:  { face: "Newsreader" > serif-text, size: 96, weight: 400, line: 0.95 }
  headline:        { face: "Newsreader" > serif-text, size: 88, weight: 400, line: 0.95 }
  ed-callout:      { face: "Newsreader" > serif-text, size: 50, weight: 400, style: italic, line: 1.1 }
  row-headline:    { face: "Newsreader" > serif-text, size: 40, weight: 400, line: 1.05 }
  table-name:      { face: "Newsreader" > serif-text, size: 36, weight: 400, line: 1.15 }
  body-lede:       { face: "Hanken Grotesk" > sans, size: 36, weight: 400, line: 1.5 }
  body:            { face: "Hanken Grotesk" > sans, size: 32, weight: 400, line: 1.5 }
  micro-strong:    { face: "Hanken Grotesk" > sans, size: 26, weight: 600, tracking: 0.18em }
  micro:           { face: "Hanken Grotesk" > sans, size: 22, weight: 600, tracking: 0.16em }
  mono-tag:        { face: "DM Mono" > mono, size: 24, weight: 400, tracking: 0.05em }
  mono-chrome:     { face: "DM Mono" > mono, size: 22, weight: 400, tracking: 0.06em }
  cjk:             { display: song 700, body: hei 400 }
space: { edge: 80, top: 134, bottom: 115, gap: 38, cell: 38, rule: 2, rule-soft: 1 }
```

Faces: use the named face when installed or vendored in `assets/fonts/`,
otherwise the stack after `>`. Newsreader is a news text serif, so it takes
serif-text, not the Didot stack; it stays 400 in cobalt and size alone ranks.

## Frame craft

- Squint: one Newsreader moment, usually display-hero or vbig-numeral, dominates
  at 3–6× its neighbor; size ranks, weight never does.
- Silence: cover, chapter, quote and colophon stay 45–60% empty with the grid
  showing; the index ledger and data frame are dense by quiet repetition.
- Restraint: cream and cobalt, never a second hue; one glitch column and at most
  one qr-block per declarative frame. Emphasis is size, the serif, a delta or opacity.

## Components

- **graph-grid**: 1px lines in `grid` on 38px cells behind every frame; never off.
- **hairlines**: two 2px ink rules ~58px in from top and bottom, inset 80px at the
  sides, framing every composition.
- **page-chrome**: mono-chrome in ink above the bottom hairline: page number at
  right, a nav or meta hint at left. The only persistent chrome.
- **pixel-glitch**: a stair-stepped column 270–576px wide, full height, of
  vertical scanlines (2px ink, 6px gap) on paper; above the grid, under the
  headline. Right on cover and data, left on chapter and colophon.
- **qr-block**: an 8×8 mosaic 58–173px square, ink cells on, grid tint off, on
  paper with a 2px paper outline for legibility, not a shadow. Corner punctuation.
- **topbar-rule**: a headline-index title and a mono-tag over a 2px ink rule; the
  header of index, data and table frames.
- **ledger-row**: mono number · Newsreader table-name · Hanken body · mono delta
  (↑ ↓ —), 1px ink-faint dividers under a 2px ink header rule.
- **pixel-stack-bar**: grid-unit cells stacked on a 2px ink baseline, ink on,
  grid tint off, mono-chrome ticks below; it echoes the glitch.
- **vstack-label**: mono-chrome set vertically along a frame edge.

## Frame types

1. **Hero cover** — a ~500px glitch column at right, a qr-block top right; a one-
   or two-line display-hero in cobalt at left, an italic ed-callout in ink-soft
   under it, a micro kicker and mono meta above. ~45% open; readable at frame 0.
2. **Index ledger** — taller top and bottom pads; a topbar-rule over 4–6 ledger
   rows. Delta arrows are the only emphasis. The dense frame; no glitch.
3. **Chapter opener** — a ~270px glitch at left in low opacity, a mono chapter
   index over a display-chapter title, an optional lede ≤806px wide. ~60% open.
4. **Data frame** — a topbar-rule with a mono figure tag over 6–8 pixel-stack-bars
   on the baseline with mono ticks. Cobalt cells are the only accent.
5. **Manifesto / quote** — centered: a micro kicker, a two- or three-line
   display-quote, a 1px ink attribution rule and a mono byline. ~55% open.
6. **Colophon** — the glitch at left, mirroring the cover; a right-aligned
   display-closing under a micro kicker; 3–4 columns of mono credits at the foot.

## Motion

- Verbs: rules draw, the glitch steps in, QR cells switch on, cells stack, lines unmask.
- Grid, hairlines and page chrome are on frame 0 and never move; chapters cut hard
  on the downbeat, changing only what sits on the paper.
- Newsreader lines reveal by a baseline mask, 0.6–0.7s `power3.out`, a line per
  beat; the ed-callout fades in over 0.4s half a beat later.
- The glitch builds by its stair steps in 0.5s on `steps(6)`; QR cells switch on
  in a fixed shuffled order over 0.4s on `steps(8)`.
- Topbar and attribution rules draw in 0.5s `power2.inOut`; ledger rows follow
  0.1s apart, rising 8px; delta arrows land last, on the beat.
- The baseline draws in 0.4s, then each bar fills cell by cell on `steps(n)`
  (n = its cells) over 0.6–0.8s, 0.1s apart.
- Never: a second hue or color shift, blur, bounce, rotation, a moving grid.

## Do and don't

- Do keep the graph-grid, both hairlines and page chrome on every frame.
- Do set Newsreader at 400 in cobalt, negative-tracked on display; size ranks.
- Do render data as pixel-stack cells; give declarative frames a glitch and a QR.
- Do keep declarative frames sparse, index and data dense; cover, index and
  chapter left, quote centered, colophon right-aligned.
- Don't add a second ink, bold the serif, round a corner, draw a circle, cast a
  shadow (the QR outline is not one) or run a headline edge to edge.
- Copy keeps its approved casing; labels get their look from Hanken 600 and
  0.16–0.18em tracking (CJK has no case).

## 9:16 and 1:1

- Cover: headline on top, glitch as a full-width band on 9:16; glitch lower on 1:1.
- Ledger: fewer rows on 9:16, two columns drop to one on 1:1. Chapter: title on top.
- Data: 4–5 taller bars on 9:16, a square chart on 1:1; quote centered and taller.
- Colophon: stacked, glitch on top on 9:16; centered on 1:1. Grid and rules hold.

## Self-check before snapshot

- One Newsreader moment dominates; declarative frames 45–60% open.
- Cream and cobalt only; grid on, both hairlines on, page chrome above the rule.
- No shadow (QR outline aside), no rounded corner, no circle.
- Copy keeps its approved casing; nothing below 22px.
- Every figure, name and logo traces to the brief; otherwise leave it out. Bar
  heights and deltas too; catalogue ordinals (001, 002) may be decorative.

# code-editorial — warm brand book with a code surface

Adapted from the HyperFrames frame preset `code-editorial` (heygen-com/hyperframes,
Apache-2.0, see `LICENSE-hyperframes.txt`). Changed for Orkas VideoStudio: local
font stacks with CJK faces, px sizes with the 22px floor, approved-copy casing,
and a motion section.

Pick it when the subject is considered, literary and developer-facing: a code
change, release or developer doc that wants editorial calm and a first-class
code surface. Changelogs, pull-request walkthroughs, SDK and API launches.
Failure looks like an IDE screenshot on pure white, or coral turning up thrice.

## Tokens

```yaml
colors:             # keep the roles; remap by role (see design-presets.md)
  ink: "#141413"         # ink: headlines and body on cream and tile
  cream: "#FAF9F5"       # canvas: the default ground; also type on navy
  tile: "#EFE9DE"        # surface: content half a step darker
  tile-strong: "#ECE3D4" # surface: the stronger step
  coral: "#CC785C"       # accent: one moment per frame, and the ✱ mark
  navy: "#181715"        # deep: code surface body, gravity grounds
  navy-soft: "#1F1E1B"   # deep: dark cards
  navy-elev: "#252320"   # deep, raised: code title bar and status strip
syntax: { string: "#5DB8A6", number: "#E8A55A", success: "#5DB872", warn: "#C64545" } # fixed; keywords coral; never remapped
lines:  { hairline: "ink at 12%", hairline-strong: "ink at 20%", dark: "cream at 14%, on navy" }
shadow: { card: "0 1px 3px ink at 8%, 0 4px 16px ink at 4%" } # the only shadow, used rarely
type:                # px on 1920×1080
  display-cover:  { face: "EB Garamond" > serif-text, size: 190, weight: 400, line: 0.98, tracking: -0.028em }
  number-hero:    { face: "EB Garamond" > serif-text, size: 180, weight: 400, line: 0.95, tracking: -0.025em }
  display:        { face: "EB Garamond" > serif-text, size: 140, weight: 400, line: 1.02, tracking: -0.022em }
  display-italic: { face: "EB Garamond" > serif-text, size: 129, weight: 400, style: italic, line: 1.05, tracking: -0.012em }
  quote-pull:     { face: "EB Garamond" > serif-text, size: 96, weight: 400, style: italic, line: 1.12, tracking: -0.012em }
  headline:       { face: "EB Garamond" > serif-text, size: 88, weight: 400, line: 1.06, tracking: -0.018em }
  card-title:     { face: "Inter" > sans, size: 44, weight: 500, line: 1.25, tracking: -0.005em }
  lead:           { face: "Inter" > sans, size: 40, weight: 400, line: 1.5 }
  body:           { face: "Inter" > sans, size: 29, weight: 400, line: 1.5 }
  button:         { face: "Inter" > sans, size: 28, weight: 500, line: 1.0 }
  tag:            { face: "Inter" > sans, size: 26, weight: 500, tracking: 0.18em }
  number-unit:    { face: "JetBrains Mono" > mono, size: 40, weight: 500, line: 1.0 }
  code:           { face: "JetBrains Mono" > mono, size: 32, weight: 400, line: 1.6 }
  kicker:         { face: "JetBrains Mono" > mono, size: 28, weight: 500, tracking: 0.16em }
  mono-label:     { face: "JetBrains Mono" > mono, size: 26, weight: 500, tracking: 0.02em }

```

Faces: use the named face when installed or vendored in `assets/fonts/`, otherwise
the stack after `>`. EB Garamond is warm old-style: serif-text, never Didot or sans;
display stays 400, italic voices a stance; CJK in mono kickers falls back to hei.

## Frame craft

- Squint: one EB Garamond display moment dominates at 3–6× its neighbor.
- Trinity: cream or tile ground, ink voice, coral exactly once per frame; warm
  navy only as the code surface or a gravity ground. No cool gray, pure white,
  pure black or fourth hue.
- Restraint: lift is a 1px hairline plus, rarely, the one card shadow; a tile on
  cream reads raised by its warm half-step. Density is free, as content wants.

## Components

- **card-hairline**: cream or tile, 12px radius, 1px hairline and the card shadow;
  card-title over body. Never a heavy drop, glow or gradient.
- **kicker-spike**: a coral ✱ then 2–5 indexical words in the mono kicker; never a
  sentence, never without the ✱.
- **coral-callout**: the one coral moment, 8px radius: a coral field with cream
  button or headline type, or cream with a coral edge; CTA, inline link or band.
- **number-lockup**: a number-hero figure with a mono number-unit beside it (200K,
  +1,204, −318, 17 files); serif figure, unit always mono.
- **pull-quote**: quote-pull italic (a commit message, a reviewer's line, the
  thesis) with a tag cite under it.
- **section-rule**: a 1px hairline, dark variant on navy; the only separator. A
  coral 1px rule may draw on to open a section. Never 2px or more.
- **code-surface**: a navy panel, 8px radius, dark 1px border, a navy-elev title bar
  (filename in mono-label) and status strip; cream `code` with coral keywords, teal
  strings, amber numbers. Real code from the diff or brief; this is its frame.
- **spike-mark**: the ✱ glyph (U+2731), always coral; the brand mark.

## Frame types

1. **Cover** — cream, 80px edge; a kicker-spike over a two- or three-line
   display-cover in ink, a lead, a mono-label index strip (repo · branch, or
   product · version) along an edge. The ✱ is the one coral. Readable at frame 0.
2. **Statement** — cream, or navy for gravity; a kicker and one two-line display
   sentence, display-italic for a stance. No accent, or one coral word.
3. **Code surface** — cream framing the code-surface (diff, before-and-after or typed
   snippet); outside it one coral cue such as a +/− gutter mark. The dense frame.
4. **Number / impact** — a kicker, a number-lockup over a 1px rule, a lead or
   caption; the figure in ink, at most the unit in coral.
5. **Pull-quote** — a kicker, a quote-pull, a tag cite (name · role) beneath.
6. **Closing / CTA** — cream or navy; a short display sign-off, the coral-callout,
   and for a shipped-by close a row of hairline-ringed avatars with mono names.

## Motion

- Verbs: lines dissolve in, code types on, numbers count up, a coral rule draws.
- Serif display fades up 16px in 0.6s `power2.out`, a line per beat; on the cover
  it is set from frame 0 and only the kicker and lead arrive.
- Code types on two lines per beat, each wiping in over 0.2s `none`, diff lines
  taking their gutter mark as they land; the panel is already in place.
- A number-lockup counts up to the brief's value in 0.8s `power2.out`; the unit holds.
- The coral section-rule is the only draw-on, 0.5s `power1.inOut`; the ✱ fades in
  and scales 0.92→1 in 0.4s `power2.out` on one emphasis beat per scene.
- Chapters cross-dissolve in 0.3s on the downbeat, cream to navy included.
- Never: overshoot, bounce, elastic or `back` eases, a spinning ✱, glow, tilt.

## Do and don't

- Do stand frames on cream, gather content on a tile half-step, lead with one focal.
- Do set EB Garamond 400 display, Inter 400 body, mono kickers (opened by ✱) and code.
- Do ration coral to one moment a frame; lift with a hairline and one soft shadow at
  most; keep navy for code and gravity grounds; pair figures with a mono unit.
- Don't use pure white, cool gray, pure black or a fourth hue; keep syntax colors in
  the panel; no heavy shadow, glow, gradient, tilt or square corner.
- Don't set a sans headline, a serif label or unit, or coral headline or body text.
- Copy keeps its approved casing, display included; kickers and tags get their look
  from mono or Inter 500 and 0.16–0.18em tracking (CJK has no case).

## 9:16 and 1:1

- Cover: display on top, index below on 9:16; index in a corner on 1:1.
- Statement, quote and number: stacked, taller on 9:16; centered on 1:1.
- Code surface: taller with fewer lines on 9:16, square and centered on 1:1; the
  hairline and mono chrome stay. Closing: avatars wrap below, never shrink.

## Self-check before snapshot

- One EB Garamond moment dominates; coral exactly once; navy only for code or gravity.
- 1px hairlines, one soft shadow at most, 6/8/12px radii; every figure has a mono unit.
- Copy keeps its approved casing; nothing below 22px.
- Every figure, name and logo traces to the brief; otherwise leave it out. Diffs,
  file counts and branches come from the real change; avatars only from supplied images.

Faces: use the named face when installed or vendored in `assets/fonts/`, otherwise the
stack after `>`. Bebas Neue stays 400. Display roles never take the sans, body never the
condensed face. Copy keeps its approved casing; height, condensed width and the 1–12px
tracking carry the poster, and CJK has no case.

## Frame craft

- Squint: one element dominates at 3–6× its neighbor: a hero-title, a jumbo-feature or a
  wallpaper numeral behind a region's title. Never two rival headlines.
- Silence: regions stay 40–55% empty; the catalog is the one dense frame. A thin coral
  region gets a wallpaper numeral, not more copy.
- Restraint: coral is an accent or one full region per frame, never both at full
  strength. One giant mark per quote. Type on coral is ink, never white.

## Components

- **region-split**: two or three solid surfaces at a hard edge, in rows 38/62 or columns
  40/60 or 50/50, 0 radius. The join is the layout; no gradient, no rounded seam.
- **diagonal-hatch**: `repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, transparent 0 20px, rgba(0,0,0,.06)
  20px 40px)` on every coral region; variants −45° at 30/60px, vertical at 60/62px in 10%.
- **background-numeral**: 192px in 12% ink behind a coral region's title. **giant-mark**:
  a 269px quote mark or glyph in 35% ink inside a coral region. Wallpaper, not content.
- **card**: white, a 5px coral top border as its only chrome, 0 radius, no shadow;
  holds a **card-icon** (48px coral square, one white glyph), card-title, body, card-stat.
- **sidebar-item**: white with a 4px coral left border; sidebar-value over a label.
- **accent-line**: a 77×5px coral rule under a headline; 60×4px on closing frames.
- **timeline**: a 4px ink line with a dashed tail; 20px coral nodes on cream halos.
- **info-bar**: a cream-dark band under a feature region, bar-title left, meta right.

## Frame types

1. **Region-split cover** — 38/62 rows: a hatched coral band with a wallpaper numeral,
   brand left and meta right, over cream. A two-line ink hero-title left in the cream
   field, its second line coral; the field about 45% empty. Readable at frame 0.
2. **Feature stat** — full hatched coral. An ink stat-numeral, jumbo-feature or two-line
   headline on the left, a wallpaper numeral behind, an ink label above, an optional
   body-light line within 845px. About 40% open.
3. **Quote layout** — 40/60: a hatched coral panel with a giant-mark beside a black panel
   holding a 2–3 line body-light quote in cream; a 60×4 accent-line over the attribution.
4. **Closing plate** — cream over a hatched coral foot band. A two-line ink sign-off,
   centered between an eyebrow and an accent-line. About 55% empty.
5. **Three-column catalog** — cream or black, 96px sides. A centered section-headline
   over three cards. The dense frame; coral tops and icons are its only accent.
6. **Timeline** — cream. A section-headline over the timeline, 4–5 nodes with condensed
   labels. Standard density.

## Motion

- Verbs: regions slam in, lines punch up, rules extend, numerals drift, nodes stamp on.
- A coral region wipes in from its own edge in 0.3–0.4s `expo.out`; the edge stays sharp.
- Condensed lines punch up through a baseline mask, 0.3s `power4.out`, one per beat
  (0.5s at 120 BPM). Stat numerals cut on whole, on the beat.
- Wallpaper numerals drift 2–3% over the scene, `sine.inOut`; the hatch slides one 40px
  period, `none`.
- Rules and card tops extend from the left in 0.25s `power3.out`, cards 0.12s apart. The
  timeline draws in 0.8s `power2.inOut`, nodes stamping on (scale 0→1, 0.2s) as it passes.
- Chapters hard-cut on the downbeat; a split may trade sides across the cut. The cover's
  split, band and hero-title stand at frame 0; only meta and texture move.
- Never: crossfades, feathered wipes, shadows, rotation, bounce.

## Do and don't

- Do compose with two or three of coral, ink and cream meeting at hard edges.
- Do let tracking carry the display (2px standard, 4px hero, 12px jumbo), not casing.
- Do set eyebrows coral on cream or ink, ink on coral; headlines ink on cream or coral,
  cream on ink.
- Do hatch every coral region; fill a thin one with a wallpaper numeral or giant mark.
- Do center sign-offs and catalog heads; set features and quotes left or in a split.
- Don't add a fourth surface, shadows or rounded rectangles; circles are timeline nodes.
- Don't set white headlines on coral or gray headlines anywhere; gray is body and meta.
- Don't soften an edge with a gradient (one 135° coral-dark → coral feature region is
  the exception); don't run a headline edge to edge.

## 9:16 and 1:1

- Cover: a taller band with the title below on 9:16; 40/60, title lower, on 1:1.
- Feature stat: figure on top, numeral behind on 9:16; centered on 1:1.
- Quote stacks on both, mark panel over quote. Closer: taller band on 9:16, centered on 1:1.
- Catalog: three stacked on 9:16, 2+1 on 1:1. Timeline: vertical on 9:16, compact on 1:1.
- Condensed display sets about 20% wider in CJK; re-break lines for each ratio.

## Self-check before snapshot

- One focal per region at 3–5×; sparse frames 40–55% empty, only the catalog dense.
- Two or three surfaces at hard edges, hatch on every coral region, ink on coral.
- No shadow, no rounded rectangle; anchors vary, never three alike in a row.
- Copy keeps its approved casing; nothing below 22px.
- Every figure, name and logo traces to the brief; otherwise leave it out.

# creative-mode — neo-brutalist editorial poster

Adapted from the HyperFrames frame preset `creative-mode` (heygen-com/hyperframes,
Apache-2.0, see `LICENSE-hyperframes.txt`). Changed for Orkas VideoStudio: local
font stacks with CJK faces, px sizes with the 22px floor, approved-copy casing,
and a motion section.

Pick it when the brand wants editorial presence and geometric confidence: sparse,
graphic, punchy but restrained, like a Risograph poster or a punk-zine spread. Flat
ink-bordered blocks, one big claim, a lot of cream. Indie tools, developer products.
Failure looks like a rounded, soft-shadowed SaaS feature grid.

## Tokens

```yaml
colors:             # keep the roles; remap by role (see design-presets.md)
  cream: "#EFE9D9"      # canvas: the ground on nearly every frame
  cream-2: "#E4DCC4"    # surface: table fill, block-on-block contrast
  ink: "#0F0F0F"        # ink: every border, rule and line of type on cream
  ink-2: "#2A2A2A"      # deep variant: secondary dark fills
  green: "#1F8A4C"      # accent: cell and step fills; the closing-plate ground, once
  green-dark: "#136636" # green's deep variant
  pink: "#F06CA8"       # accent: marker block, stamp, winning column
  pink-dark: "#D14E8B"  # pink's deep variant
  orange: "#E85A1F"     # accent: fills, and the hard offset shadow
  yellow: "#F5C518"     # accent: rotated badge, decorative circle
type:                # px on 1920×1080; Archivo Black is one black cut at 400
  display-hero:  { face: "Archivo Black" > sans, size: 298, weight: 400, line: 0.84, tracking: -0.02em }
  display-xl:    { face: "Archivo Black" > sans, size: 211, weight: 400, line: 0.9, tracking: -0.01em }
  display-lg:    { face: "Archivo Black" > sans, size: 154, weight: 400, line: 0.9, tracking: -0.01em }
  step-num:      { face: "Archivo Black" > sans, size: 134, weight: 400, line: 0.85 }
  stat-num:      { face: "Archivo Black" > sans, size: 123, weight: 400, line: 0.88 }
  display-head:  { face: "Archivo Black" > sans, size: 81, weight: 400, line: 0.92, tracking: -0.01em }
  marker:        { face: "Archivo Black" > sans, size: 46, weight: 400, line: 1.0 }
  stamp-num:     { face: "Archivo Black" > sans, size: 42, weight: 400, line: 0.9 }
  step-title:    { face: "Archivo Black" > sans, size: 34, weight: 400, line: 1.0 }
  badge-label:   { face: "Archivo Black" > sans, size: 28, weight: 400 }
  table-head:    { face: "Archivo Black" > sans, size: 28, weight: 400 }
  body-lg:       { face: "Space Grotesk" > sans, size: 32, weight: 400, line: 1.4 }

  mono-kicker:   { face: "JetBrains Mono" > mono, size: 24, weight: 400, tracking: 0.14em }
  mono-label:    { face: "JetBrains Mono" > mono, size: 24, weight: 400, tracking: 0.06em }

```

Faces: use the named face when installed or vendored in `assets/fonts/`, otherwise the
stack after `>`; on the `sans` stack set the Archivo Black roles at 800 so the mass holds.
Copy keeps its approved casing: black weight, the 0.84–0.92 line and tight tracking carry
the poster, and CJK has no case. Hanzi display lines need a line height of 1.05 or more.

## Frame craft

- Squint: exactly one element dominates, 3–6× its nearest neighbor, a chasm rather than
  a ramp: the display-hero or display-xl claim, or a stat-num.
- Silence: cover, claim and closer stay 45–60% empty; only the stat grid and the ledger
  run dense. Never pad a sparse frame to make it look finished.
- Restraint: per frame, at most one hard offset shadow and two or three accents, never
  all four. Green as a ground appears once, on the closing plate.

## Components

- **frame-chrome**: a mono topbar 48px from the top (label left, a 999px pill with a 2px
  ink stroke right) and a footer 48px from the bottom (descriptor left, `NN • NN` counter
  right, a 10px ink dot between), inset 64px; dropped only against a full-bleed wordmark.
- **stat-cell**: a flat green, pink, orange or cream tile, 4px ink border, square, 32px
  padding, stat-num over a mono-label; cream type on accents, ink on cream. No shadow.
- **step-card**: the same 4px square card with a giant step-num, step-title and body-md;
  fills alternate cream with pink, yellow and green, and the run ends on green.
- **marker-block**: pink, ink marker type, 4px ink border, and the signature shadow
  `24px 24px 0 orange, 24px 24px 0 4px ink`. Diagram stacks may use an 18px ink offset.
- **kicker-block**: cream mono-kicker on an ink chip, padding 10px 18px, square.
- **badge-rotated**: yellow, 4px ink border, badge-label type, turned −4°.
- **pill-badge**: cream, 2px ink border, 999px radius, mono-label; the one rounded box.
- **stamp**: a pink square about 346px, 4px cream border, a cream circular inner ring
  around stamp-num, turned −6°. The closing seal.
- **comparison-table**: cream-2, 4px ink outer border, 3px ink inner rules, an ink head
  row with cream table-head labels; one pink or green column fill marks the winner.
- **decorative-circle**: a yellow disc, 4px ink border, against a green panel or off a corner.

## Frame types

1. **Wordmark cover** — cream. A two-line display-hero wordmark centered, its second line
   pink or orange; full chrome with a `01 • NN` footer; one decorative-circle may bleed
   off a corner. About 55% empty; readable at frame 0.
2. **Big claim** — a full-bleed pink or orange ground (green stays with the closer). A
   2–3 line ink claim at display-xl or display-lg, left and vertically centered, a
   kicker-block above. No second accent; about 45% open.
3. **Stat grid** — cream. A centered display-head over green, pink and orange stat-cells,
   the one place three accents sit together. About 25% open; the dense frame.
4. **Closing plate** — green, its only use as a ground. A two-line cream display-lg
   sign-off centered, cream chrome, one pink stamp in a corner. About 55% empty.
5. **Featured marker** — cream. The marker-block and its shadow off-center, an optional
   body-md line beside it. About 50% open.
6. **Comparison ledger** — cream, 96px gutter. The full-width table with one filled
   winning column; the second dense frame.

## Motion

- Verbs: blocks slam, shadows snap out, stamps thump, cells cut on, chrome ticks over.
- Blocks slam in from 40–60px off their rest in 0.25–0.35s `power4.out`; no overshoot, no fade.
- The marker-block lands flat, then its shadow snaps out to 24px in 0.2s `power3.out` on
  the next beat (one beat = 0.5s at 120 BPM); on an accent beat it may press into it.
- Stat cells and step cards cut on one per beat, left to right; figures arrive whole.
- Badge and stamp thump from scale 1.3 to 1 in 0.25s `power4.out`, already at −4°/−6°.
- Chapters and ground swaps hard-cut on the downbeat. The cover wordmark is set at
  frame 0; chrome, pill and circle arrive within 0.6s.
- Never: blur, crossfades, soft eases on a slam, elastic wobble, two shadows moving.

## Do and don't

- Do build each frame on one idea, its focal element 3–5× the neighbors.
- Do center cover, stat grid and closer; anchor claim, marker and ledger left or off-center.
- Do keep sparse frames 45–60% empty with two or three accents; green waits for the close.
- Do spend the hard shadow on one block per frame; size Archivo Black to its measure.
- Don't round any corner but the pill's; no gradient, blur or glow.
- Don't track Archivo Black wider than −0.01em; no fifth accent, no pure white.
- Don't center body copy or set labels outside mono; don't run a headline edge to edge.

## 9:16 and 1:1

- Cover: stacked taller, circle on top on 9:16; centered and tighter on 1:1.
- Claim: at the top of the full accent on 9:16, centered on 1:1. Closer: stamp below on 9:16.
- Stat grid: three stacked on 9:16; 2×2 on 1:1, a fourth cell only for a fourth figure.
- Marker: centered, the shadow falling below on 9:16. Ledger: fewer columns, two on 1:1.
- Chrome keeps its 64px inset on the short edge in every ratio.

## Self-check before snapshot

- One element dominates at 3–5×; sparse frames 45–60% empty, only grid and ledger dense.
- Two or three accents per frame, never four; a green ground only on the closer.
- No blur, one hard shadow at most, square corners but the pill, rotation only −4°/−6°.
- Copy keeps its approved casing; nothing below 22px.
- Every figure, name and logo traces to the brief; otherwise leave it out.

Adapted from the HyperFrames frame preset `daisy-days` (heygen-com/hyperframes,
Apache-2.0, see `LICENSE-hyperframes.txt`). Changed for Orkas VideoStudio: local
font stacks with CJK faces, px sizes with the 22px floor, approved-copy casing,
and a motion section.

Pick it when the brand wants warmth and whimsy: playful, childlike, sticker-sheet
kawaii, like a children's picture book. Kids' and family products, learning apps,
playful consumer brands, seasonal campaigns.
Failure looks like a flat corporate slide: square corners, blurred shadows, bare corners.

## Tokens

```yaml
colors:             # keep the roles; remap by role (see design-presets.md)
  cream: "#F5F0E6"      # canvas: the default ground
  turquoise: "#7ECDC0"  # surface: saturated ground (cover), marker fill
  soft-pink: "#F7C8D4"  # surface: quote ground, quote-mark fill
  butter: "#FDE68A"     # surface: badge-pill, bullet dots
  mint: "#A8E6CF"       # surface: marker fill, ground
  lavender: "#D4A5E8"   # surface: closing ground, marker fill
  peach: "#FFCBA4"      # surface: process ground
  sky: "#A8D8F0"        # surface: marker fill, ground
  coral: "#F8635F"      # accent: small markers only, never a ground
  text-dark: "#2D2D2D"  # ink: every outline and shadow, headlines on cream
  text-muted: "#6B6B6B" # muted ink: meta on cream or white only
  white: "#FFFFFF"      # surface: card fill; headline type on saturated grounds

  display:       { face: "Fredoka One" > sans, size: 125, line: 1.1, tracking: 0.02em }
  headline:      { face: "Fredoka One" > sans, size: 86, line: 1.1, tracking: 0.02em }
  title:         { face: "Fredoka One" > sans, size: 58, line: 1.15, tracking: 0.02em }
  quote:         { face: "Fredoka One" > sans, size: 50, line: 1.35 }
  subtitle:      { face: "Fredoka One" > sans, size: 35, line: 1.2, tracking: 0.02em }
  label-display: { face: "Fredoka One" > sans, size: 25, line: 1.3, tracking: 0.02em }
  badge:         { face: "Fredoka One" > sans, size: 22, tracking: 0.02em }
  body:          { face: "Quicksand" > sans, size: 32, weight: 500, line: 1.6 }
  body-strong:   { face: "Quicksand" > sans, size: 32, weight: 600, line: 1.5 }
  meta:          { face: "Quicksand" > sans, size: 24, weight: 600, line: 1.45 }
  cjk:           { display: hei 600, body: hei 500 }
line: { primary: 3px text-dark, thin: 2px text-dark, ornament: 2.1px text-dark }
shadow: { default: "6px 6px 0 text-dark", small: "4px 4px 0 text-dark",
          headline: "3px 3px 0 text-dark", headline-soft: "3px 3px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.2)" }

```

Faces: use the named face when installed or vendored in `assets/fonts/`, otherwise the
stack after `>`. Fredoka One has one weight; Fredoka at 600 is its twin, so vendor that
when it is missing. On the bare `sans` stack set display at 700 and check the inspect
frame. Fredoka is never italic or underlined; Quicksand stays 500–700; roles never swap.

## Frame craft

- Squint: one Fredoka headline or one content card dominates at 3–6× its neighbor.
- Silence: one content container per frame, ringed by an ornament wreath; bare corners
  read as broken. The info-card grid is the one dense frame.
- Restraint: cream or one pastel ground per frame; coral only on small markers; charcoal
  for every border and shadow; no ninth color.

## Components

- **card**: white, 3px charcoal border, 20px radius (28px featured), 6px charcoal offset.
  The universal container, white on any ground.
- **framed-header**: a pastel cap flush on a white body inside one continuous 3px border,
  28px radius, one 6px shadow for the whole unit.
- **badge-pill**: butter, 3px border, 50px radius, badge type, 4px shadow, on one line.
- **circle-marker**: an outlined disc (3px, 50%) in any pastel with a Fredoka numeral,
  white on most fills, charcoal on butter; bullet 20, icon 44, dot 48, step 90px, and
  steps take the 4px shadow.
- **bullet-dot**: a 20px butter disc, 2px charcoal outline, 4px below the line's top.
  Lists never use glyph bullets.
- **ornament**: hand-drawn SVG daisies, stars, suns, clouds and rainbows, 2.1px charcoal
  stroke, 3–7 per frame at corners and edges, cropped by the frame, behind content.
- **quote-mark**: an oversized Fredoka quote glyph, soft-pink with a charcoal stroke.
- **text-headline-shadow**: a 3px charcoal offset under white headlines on saturated
  grounds (20% soft variant on soft-pink and mint); on cream, headlines sit flat.

## Frame types

1. **Cover** — a saturated pastel such as turquoise. A 1–2 line white display with the
   text shadow, centered under a butter badge-pill, a body line below, a counter pill;
   daisies and stars crop off the corners. Full, never crowded; readable at frame 0.
2. **Info cards** — cream. A flat charcoal headline over three white cards, each a
   circle-marker icon (turquoise, coral, lavender), title and body. The dense frame;
   only a couple of ornaments.
3. **Process steps** — peach or another pastel. A white shadowed headline over 3–4 90px
   step circles filled coral → mint → sky → lavender, joined by Fredoka arrows.
4. **Quote** — soft-pink. A white 28px card with a charcoal Fredoka quote under a big
   quote-mark, a Quicksand 700 attribution; a star or two at the corners.
5. **Framed section** — cream. One framed-header: a pastel cap with a Fredoka title over
   a white body with a butter-dot list, ornaments at the edges. Standard density.
6. **Closing** — a saturated pastel such as lavender. A badge-pill and a white shadowed
   display sign-off, centered inside a full ornament wreath.

## Motion

- Verbs: stickers pop, cards drop onto their shadows, ornaments twirl, dots stamp, steps hop.
- Cards, badges and markers pop from scale 0.6 to 1 in 0.35–0.45s `back.out(1.7)`; the
  shadow travels with its shape.
- Ornaments pop 0.08s apart with `back.out(2)`, then daisies turn 6–10° over the scene and
  stars pulse 1→1.08 on beats, `sine.inOut` (one beat = 0.5s at 120 BPM).
- List lines rise 24px over 0.4s `power2.out`, one per beat, each bullet-dot stamping in.
- Step circles hop in one per beat, 0.4s `back.out(2)`; each arrow draws in 0.3s between.
- Chapters cut on the downbeat with a ground swap, or a 0.5s `power2.inOut` pastel wipe.
- Cover and closing headlines and badges are on screen at frame 0; only ornaments move.
- Never: blur, whole-frame fades, linear slides, softening shadows, spinning type.

## Do and don't

- Do set every headline in Fredoka and every body line in Quicksand.
- Do outline every shape in 3px charcoal with a hard 6px or 4px offset; cards stay white.
- Do give headlines on saturated grounds white type and the text shadow; flat on cream.
- Do use butter-disc bullets and a 3–7 ornament wreath cropping at the corners.
- Do keep one container per frame; rotate markers coral → mint → sky → lavender → butter.
- Do center most frames; cream for dense ones, saturated for cover, quote and closer.
- Don't use square corners, blurred or rgba shadows (bar the soft text shadow), colored
  borders, a coral ground, a ninth color or a third font.
- Don't use glyph bullets, bare corners, two competing panels or edge-to-edge headlines.

## 9:16 and 1:1

- Cover, quote and closing: centered on both; taller on 9:16 with 5–7 ornaments.
- Info cards: stacked on 9:16, 2+1 on 1:1. Steps: vertical, arrows down on 9:16; 2×2 on 1:1.
- Framed section: cap and body, the body growing taller on 9:16.
- Keep the 56px edge on the short side; tight ratios lean to 5–7 ornaments.

## Self-check before snapshot

- One headline or card dominates; one container in its wreath; only info cards dense.
- Cream or one pastel ground; coral markers only; text-muted only on cream or white.
- 3px outline and hard offset on every raised shape, no blur; 3–7 ornaments; disc bullets.
- Copy keeps its approved casing; nothing below 22px.
- Every figure, name and logo traces to the brief; otherwise leave it out.

```yaml
  title-card:       { face: "Source Serif 4" > serif-text, size: 67, weight: 500, line: 0.96, tracking: -0.01em }
  title-card-sm:    { face: "Source Serif 4" > serif-text, size: 56, weight: 500, line: 0.98, tracking: -0.01em }
  name:             { face: "Source Serif 4" > serif-text, size: 44, weight: 600, line: 1.0 }
  lede:             { face: "Source Serif 4" > serif-text, size: 36, weight: 400, line: 1.38 }
  body:             { face: "Source Serif 4" > serif-text, size: 30, weight: 400, line: 1.38 }
  body-card:        { face: "Source Serif 4" > serif-text, size: 28, weight: 400, line: 1.34 }
  label:            { face: "JetBrains Mono" > mono, size: 26, weight: 500, tracking: 0.18em }
  caption-mono:     { face: "JetBrains Mono" > mono, size: 24, weight: 500, tracking: 0.14em }
  cjk:              { display: song 500, body: song 400, chrome: hei 500 }
space: { edge: 96, rule: 2, rule-card: 2.5, radius-card: 6, radius-step: 8 }
```

Faces: use the named face when installed or vendored in `assets/fonts/`, otherwise the
stack after `>`. Vendor Source Serif 4 with its optical-size axis (`font-optical-sizing:
auto`) or display and body flatten into one cut. Display 500, body 400, name 600; on
`serif-text` 500 falls to regular, never to bold. Mono chrome keeps the copy's approved
casing; weight 500 and the 0.14–0.18em tracking carry the labels, and CJK has no case.

## Frame craft

- Squint: one serif moment dominates at 3–6× its neighbor; the surface block draws the eye.
- Silence: one subject per frame in deep negative space; only the topic-tile and step
  grids run dense.
- Restraint: two surface tones per frame at most, three reads loud. Serif 500 for
  display, 400 for body; the green ground is kept for moments of weight.

## Components

- **topbar**: a mono label left, a monogram-circle or ordinal counter right, along the top
  inside the 96px edge. On every frame; without it a frame looks untreated.
- **footline**: two caption-mono strings at opposite ends of the bottom edge; on cover,
  data and summary frames.
- **monogram-circle**: 130px, 2px pink border, a mono monogram inside. The identity
  stamp, cover and summary only, and the only full round.
- **topic-tile**: 6px radius, no shadow; caption-mono ordinal, title-card-sm title, mono
  foot. Fills rotate green with pink type, pink with green-deep, green-lite with pink,
  cream-2 with a 2px green border and green type; no fill repeats in a grid.
- **step-tile**: 8px radius, 2.5px border; cream with a green border, green, or pink; a
  mono ordinal, title-card title, body-card copy, a mono marker over a top rule.
- **kpi-block**: caption-mono tag, stat-figure with its unit, a body line, under a 2px rule.
- **meta-dl**: a three-column term-and-value grid under a 2px green rule; mono terms.
- **bar**: 56px wide in pink, cream or green, 3px 3px 0 0 corners, a mono value above.
- **rule-thin**: 2px in the region's accent (green on cream, pink on green, green-deep on
  pink). The only separator; never 1px, never 3px or more.

## Frame types

1. **Cover** — green. A two-line pink display-hero, left, one word in cream; a lede, the
   topbar with label and monogram-circle, a footline. About 50% open; readable at frame 0.
2. **Topic tiles** — cream. A headline-xl over three or four topic tiles in three of the
   four fills, none repeated. The dense frame.
3. **KPI stat** — green. A kpi-block with a 221px pink stat-figure and unit over a 2px
   pink rule; topbar and footline. About 55% open.
4. **Statement** — cream, generous edge. A two-line green display, left, the 600 name and
   a caption-mono role beneath. No accent; the serif carries it. About 55% open.
5. **Step framework** — cream or green. A headline over three or four step-tiles with
   67px titles, fills rotating through the three variants. Standard density.
6. **Chart** — green. A headline over 56px pink, cream and green bars on 2px axis rules
   with mono ticks, an optional meta-dl below. Standard density.

## Motion

- Verbs: lines rise through masks, rules draw, tiles settle, bars grow, the ring draws.
- Display and headline lines reveal by a baseline mask, 0.7–0.9s `power3.out`, one line
  per beat (0.5s at 120 BPM).
- Rules draw from their start edge in 0.6s `power2.inOut`; tiles follow 0.15s apart,
  rising 16px as they fade in over 0.5s `power2.out`.
- Bars grow from the axis in 0.8s `power2.out`, 0.1s apart, values fading in as each
  lands; the stat-figure reveals whole by mask, never counting.
- The ground holds still; a display may drift 1% over the scene, `sine.inOut`.
- Chapters cut on the downbeat with a ground swap or a 0.6s `power2.inOut` mask wipe.
- The cover's display-hero and topbar are set at frame 0; lede and footline rise in over
  0.8s, and the monogram ring draws in 0.9s.
- Never: bounce, scale pops, shadows, glow, rotation, fast zooms on type.

## Do and don't

- Do run display in Source Serif 4 at 500, tight and negatively tracked; body at 400.
- Do set labels, captions, ticks and footlines in mono 500 at 0.08–0.18em.
- Do give every frame a topbar, and cover and data frames a footline.
- Do keep one dominant surface, two tones at most, and rotate tile fills without repeats.
- Do set headlines green on cream, cream or pink on green, green-deep on pink (body ink,
  cream, green-deep likewise); pink and green on each other only from 84px.
- Don't add shadow, gradient or glow; depth is color block, hairline, border against fill.
- Don't add a third face, italic, underline, serif body at 500 or mono at headline scale.
- Don't add a fourth color family, rgba surfaces, rules outside 2/2.5px, two competing
  blocks or an edge-to-edge headline.

## 9:16 and 1:1

- Cover: display on top, monogram below on 9:16; monogram to a corner on 1:1.
- Tiles and steps: stacked on 9:16; 2×2 on 1:1.
- KPI stat and statement: centered (the figure taller, the quote stacked) on 9:16 and 1:1.
- Chart: taller bars, meta stacked on 9:16; a square chart on 1:1.
- The topbar spans the top on every ratio; the 96px edge holds on the short side.

## Self-check before snapshot

- One serif moment dominates; one subject per frame, only tile and step grids dense.
- Two surface tones at most, per-surface type colors; display 500, body 400, no italic.
- No shadow or gradient; 2px rules; 6/8px radii; topbar on every frame.
- Copy keeps its approved casing; nothing below 22px.
- Every figure, name and logo traces to the brief; otherwise leave it out.

# HTML generation playbook

Use this when mapping reference frames into `art_direction` and before writing `index.html`. This is an internal authorship pass, not a user gate and not a new required project file.

## Private pre-code art direction

Use the path selected in `frontend-design`. Keep the result in the existing manifest; this pass implements its scene plan.

### Reference-led composition

For each scene about to be planned or implemented, open its saved source frame as an image with `read_files` (`metadata_only: false`) immediately before authoring. Earlier inspection receipts and plan prose do not keep the pixels visible in a later turn. Use the visible frame and mapped source time to fill the existing fields below, then write that scene description or HTML while the frame is in context:

1. **Elements and substitutions** — identify the source elements and their roles. Replace their content with confirmed target copy and explicit user changes, retaining the visual relationships.
2. **Recurring carrier** — retain the element and connections that continue between the mapped source scenes.
3. **Type hierarchy** — derive relative title/body/label scale, placement and contrast from the source while preserving approved casing.
4. **Spatial arrangement** — put named regions, relative positions and sizes, grouping and connections in `art_direction.scenes[].composition`. Record the source frame/time with this description. For example: a main card centered above three equal child cards, joined by branching lines; replace the card copy inside that arrangement. This describes a particular frame, not a theme such as "modular cards".
5. **Observed motion** — fill opening/resolved states and motion verbs from the observed changes and holds, using the declared temporal anchors. Unseen movement remains unknown under `reference-recreation`.

Build the static HTML/CSS/SVG from those mapped regions, then apply the content substitutions before adding motion. Keep the source scene sequence and layout changes within the user's preserve/may-change scope. Implementation primitives fit these regions; a new visual metaphor is an original-design decision.

### Original composition

Without a concrete reference, decide five things before coding:

1. **Material world** — list the real artifacts, surfaces, marks, diagrams, interfaces, documents, objects, or physical behaviors that belong to the topic. Prefer those over generic circles and lines.
2. **Recurring carrier** — choose one visual object that can move through the story: signal, rule, token stream, document strip, route, waveform, product surface, cursor, scale, or data mark.
3. **Type behavior** — choose how display, supporting copy, labels, and data differ through family, width, weight, scale, color, spacing, or tracking while preserving approved casing.
4. **Spatial rhythm** — alternate where the dominant mass lives. A sequence can move left-heavy → full-field → right-heavy → centered payoff; it should not reset to the same top-left title layout each time.
5. **Motion logic** — decide what information is established, explained, and resolved. Motion must change meaning or state, not merely prove that animation exists.

For every scene, internally answer:

- What single visual object explains this beat without narration?
- Where does the largest visual mass sit, and how much of the safe canvas does it occupy?
- What are the background, midground, and foreground layers?
- What is already visible on the first frame of the scene?
- What new understanding exists in the resolved frame?
- What enters from the previous scene and what leaves for the next one?
- Which primitive or custom SVG construction will implement it?

Put compact answers in the existing design contract scene fields when they help HTML execution. Do not create a separate approval artifact.

Before coding the first scene, resolve the dedicated cover contract separately: approved headline, dominant hero, at least two concrete signals of the video's real content, and a composition that still communicates at thumbnail size. Frame 0 is the exported cover, so it cannot be a generic title treatment or an incomplete tween state.

## Original composition preferences

Without a concrete reference, compose intentional video frames:

- Use asymmetric tension, scale contrast, edge anchoring, cropping, overlap, or a strong full-field structure. Do not center every object inside generous web-page whitespace.
- Let meaningful material occupy the canvas. Empty space is useful only when it creates direction, suspense, scale, or emphasis.
- Use three semantic depth layers. Background structure should belong to the subject; midground carries the main message; foreground annotations, ticks, fragments, or masks create scale and finish.
- Build one dominant focal point and one supporting focal point. Tiny labels scattered around a small diagram do not create hierarchy.
- Prefer a few large shapes and readable annotations over many small cards. At phone size, labels must remain legible and the hero graphic must still read as a silhouette.

## Opening, explanation, resolved

For both paths, keep exact words, dates, numbers, and CTA copy as real HTML. Use SVG for geometry, relationships, paths, masks, charts, and spatial systems.

Reference-led scenes take their states from the observed source. For original work, design three states:

1. **Opening** — the premise and visual identity are already visible. The first scene must never be a blank canvas waiting for a fade.
2. **Explanation** — structure, comparison, connection, or causality becomes visible in a controlled sequence.
3. **Resolved** — the completed idea holds long enough to read and should be visibly different from the opening state.

For both paths, author the resolved state first in HTML/CSS/SVG, then implement the planned opening and explanation states. For original work, choose which parts begin muted, clipped, offset, or incomplete; avoid using only container opacity.

For the first scene:

```js
// The opening composition is visible at t=0. Animate supporting structure,
// not the whole scene from a blank frame.
tl.set('#s01', { opacity: 1 }, 0)
  .fromTo('#s01 .signal',
    { strokeDashoffset: 720 },
    { strokeDashoffset: 0, duration: 1.2, ease: 'power2.out' }, 0)
  .fromTo('#s01 .annotation',
    { opacity: 0.25, y: 18 },
    { opacity: 1, y: 0, duration: 0.65, stagger: 0.08 }, 0.25);
```

For later scenes, a hard cut, wipe, carried object, or short crossfade may reveal the next scene at its start. Do not spend the first second of every scene fading an empty layout into view.

## Original scene variation

Without a concrete reference, keep typography, palette, stroke character, corner treatment, and the recurring carrier consistent. Vary two or more of these per scene:

- dominant mass position;
- full-field versus split composition;
- visual grammar: document, path, network, comparison, scale, object, quote;
- camera/framing: macro crop, overview, detail, centered payoff;
- motion behavior: draw, reveal, accumulate, transform, converge;
- relationship between text and visual: integrated, adjacent, overprinted, annotated.

Variation is structural, not a new palette or unrelated visual style every few seconds.

## Original generation-time anti-patterns

In original work, replace these before coding:

- `top-left headline + small diagram below` repeated across the sequence;
- a pure-color background with only one thin SVG group;
- four words placed around a circle as a substitute for an explanation;
- multiple diagonal lines without scale, anchors, values, or change over time;
- universal Arial/Helvetica with no meaningful role contrast;
- all scene roots fading from opacity zero;
- a final frame that is identical to the prior scene midpoint;
- arbitrary decorative particles, blobs, cards, grids, or glows unrelated to the topic.

## Initial-generation checklist

Before saving `index.html`, verify from the source itself:

- frame 0 contains the promise and a subject-specific visual signal;
- frame 0 satisfies every `art_direction.cover.content_signals` item and reads as the actual video's cover;
- reference images and videos satisfy their reproduce/edit/guide intent, protected axes, allowed changes, and layout/temporal anchors;
- scene layering follows the source, or the planned background/midground/foreground for original work;
- each scene has a large, recognizable hero visual;
- the spatial sequence follows the mapped source, or varies within the original visual system;
- opening/resolved states follow the observed changes and holds, or reveal new information in original work;
- continuity follows the source carrier, or the chosen original motif;
- typography roles differ beyond font size;
- SVG structure encodes real content rather than generic decoration;
- no remote runtime dependency is required;
- animation is deterministic and registered on the paused GSAP timeline.

# Worked composition references

Use these as reasoning examples, not layouts to copy. Preserve the method—extract subject materials, choose a carrier, vary spatial grammar, author resolved states—while changing the actual design for each brief.

## Example 1: A short history of large language models

**Weak default:** dark background, top-left heading, one generic diagram per scene, yellow circles and lines everywhere.

**Subject materials:** paper typography, token rows, attention matrices, parameter scales, chat turns, image crops, waveforms, syntax bands.

**Visual system:** near-black research desk; warm paper-white type; amber signal as the historical carrier; mint/red only for meaningful comparison. Display type is dense and editorial; labels feel measured and technical through weight, spacing, and alignment while preserving approved casing.

**Sequence:**

1. Title wall: a giant cropped `2017` sits behind the title; a Transformer paper fragment occupies the right third; the amber signal is already visible at frame 0.
2. Attention: the paper fragment expands into a full-height attention matrix; token rows activate and contextual arcs resolve over it.
3. Scaling: the same amber path becomes a measured logarithmic climb with anchored model eras, exact values, and a large terminal data mark.
4. Chat: the path straightens into a cursor rail; two oversized conversational turns displace the prior chart rather than appearing inside small UI cards.
5. Multimodal: text rows, image crop tiles, waveform bands, and code columns arrive with different material behaviors and converge into one field.
6. Payoff: the four materials remain visible inside a unified output object while the thesis resolves in large type. The final frame is not a copy of the prior midpoint.

**Why it works:** every scene uses content evidence, the amber carrier provides continuity, and the spatial mass moves from split to full-field to measured comparison to centered convergence.

## Example 2: Product feature launch

**Weak default:** floating browser card, gradient background, three benefit cards, logo and CTA.

**Subject materials:** actual product surface, cursor path, before/after states, real output, brand typography and tokens.

**Visual system:** the product itself occupies 55–75% of the frame. Supporting copy is edge-anchored and never competes with the interface. A cursor/selection path carries the story.

**Sequence:**

1. Open on the finished outcome at full scale, not a logo fade.
2. Pull back to reveal the product surface and the one action that produced it.
3. Use a cropped before/after split with one continuous cursor path crossing the divider.
4. Resolve into the product's output plus one concise proof point.

**Why it works:** the product is the hero visual; graphics explain interaction and outcome instead of wrapping the product in generic marketing decoration.

## Example 3: Data-led explainer

**Weak default:** dashboard grid with many tiny charts and metric cards.

**Subject materials:** one decisive comparison, exact values, baseline, range, annotation, category shape.

**Visual system:** one data mark dominates each scene. Supporting values are large HTML text. Grid lines and ticks are sparse, measured, and consistent.

**Sequence:**

1. Open with the surprising number as a large physical mass beside a clear denominator.
2. Reveal the baseline and comparison categories from the same origin.
3. Transform the dominant bar/path into the next scene's scale rather than cutting to a new dashboard.
4. Resolve with the implication in type while the complete chart remains visible.

**Why it works:** data has tangible visual weight; the audience sees a relationship, not a collection of interface widgets.

## Example 4: Abstract systems concept

**Weak default:** four labeled nodes around a glowing center.

**Subject materials:** pick a physical behavior that matches the argument—branching, compression, collision, sorting, accumulation, or convergence.

**Visual system:** each input has a different geometry and motion behavior. The center is not meaningful until the inputs visibly change it.

**Sequence for convergence:**

1. Inputs already occupy distinct edges of frame 0.
2. Each input crosses a measured boundary and changes form.
3. Intermediate relationships become visible through paths, masks, or shared alignment.
4. The resolved object contains recognizable traces of every input.

**Why it works:** the animation demonstrates the concept. Labels support the transformation rather than substituting for it.

## Applying the examples

Before generating HTML, write a one-line comparison internally:

```text
The weak default would be [generic composition]; this brief instead uses
[subject material] as [hero visual] and carries [recurring object] across scenes.
```

If that sentence could describe any topic, the direction is still too generic. Revise it before coding.
